definition_zh: 赤裸的；严酷的；鲜明的；完全的
definition_en: very plain and bare, harsh with nothing soft or comforting, and used to mean completely
core_image: 冬天的枯树，枝干一根不剩叶子，直直立在灰白天空下
scene: 病房的墙壁雪白，只有一张铁床，四下里空得让人心里发紧。The hospital ward was stark, with white walls and a single iron bed.
sceneCN: 这里 stark 是「简陋刺目、令人心下发紧的」（第 1 个义项：毫无装饰、赤裸得让人感到冷硬）；句意：病房的墙壁雪白，只有一张铁床，四下里空得让人心里发紧。

pos.zh: 赤裸的；毫无修饰的；严酷的；鲜明的；完全的
完全地；十足地，用于 stark naked 等搭配

derivatives.zh: 由 stark 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「鲜明地；严酷地」
由 stark 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「荒凉；严酷；鲜明」
英式口语中由 stark 加 -ers 构成，义为「一丝不挂的」

senses.title: Bare and severely plain
senses.definition: empty of decoration or comfort, so that what is left looks bare and harsh
senses.definitionCN: 没有任何装饰或舒适之物，剩下的只是赤裸、冷硬的景象
senses.example: The room was stark, with one chair and no carpet.
senses.exampleCN: 屋里空荡荡的，只有一把椅子，连地毯都没有。
senses.why: The oldest sense was rigid and unyielding, which grew into bare and stripped of everything soft.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思是僵硬、不肯弯曲，后来引申为光秃、没有任何柔软之物的样子。

senses.title: Harsh and unsparing
senses.definition: so hard and plain that no comfort or escape is offered
senses.definitionCN: 严酷直白，不给人安慰或逃避的余地
senses.example: The report paints a stark picture of rural poverty.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描绘出一幅严酷的农村贫困图景。
senses.why: What is rigid refuses to soften, so stark came to describe facts and warnings that will not be smoothed over.
senses.whyCN: 僵硬的东西不肯变软，所以 stark 也形容揭开来就不加粉饰的事实与警告。

senses.title: Clear and sharply contrasted
senses.definition: very obvious because two things differ sharply, with no middle ground
senses.definitionCN: 由于对立鲜明、没有中间地带而十分明显
senses.example: There is a stark difference between the two plans.
senses.exampleCN: 两个方案之间有悬殊的差别。
senses.why: Bareness leaves no shades to blur the edges, so a contrast or difference becomes strikingly clear.
senses.whyCN: 光秃意味着没有过渡色去打糊边缘，于是对比与差别显得格外清楚。

senses.title: Complete, as in stark naked
senses.definition: used before an adjective to mean entirely or utterly, especially in stark naked and stark raving mad
senses.definitionCN: 置于形容词前表示「完全地、十足地」，尤见于 stark naked 与 stark raving mad
senses.example: The children ran stark naked into the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们光着身子跑进海里。
senses.why: Rigid or bare became intensive, so the word now simply hammers the point without adding a new meaning.
senses.whyCN: 「僵硬、赤裸」的意味被强化为语气词，于是它只是加重语气，并未带来新的实义。

intro.en: Stark goes back to Old English stearc, meaning stiff or hard, and the modern senses of bare, harsh and complete all grow from that stiffness.
intro.cn: stark 可追溯到古英语 stearc（僵硬、坚硬），现代的「光秃、严酷、完全」诸义都从这股僵硬感长出来。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as stark shows the same stiff and rigid sense.
items.cn: 重构形式 stark 同样表示僵硬、坚硬。

items.en: Stearc means stiff, rigid, strong, and sometimes hard in manner.
items.cn: stearc 意为僵直、坚硬、强壮，有时也指态度强硬。

items.en: The spelling settles as stark and the sense of bare or plain begins to spread.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 stark，光秃、朴素的意思开始扩散。

items.en: Stark comes to mean unsoftened, severe and unsparing.
items.cn: stark 开始表示不柔和、严厉、不加宽恕。

items.en: Stark also becomes an intensive, as in stark naked, and a plain adjective of clear contrast.
items.cn: 到现代英语中，stark 也用作加强语气的成分，如 stark naked，同时成为表示鲜明对比的普通形容词。

note.en: Stark sits among Germanic stiffness words and near the plainness words bare, harsh, and absolute.
note.cn: stark 属于日耳曼语中表示僵硬的词族，同时靠近 bare、harsh、absolute 这些与「裸露、严酷、绝对」有关的词。

entries.definition: in a plain and clear way
entries.definitionCN: 由 stark 加 -ly 构成，义为「鲜明地；严酷地」

entries.definition: the quality of being bare and harsh
entries.definitionCN: 由 stark 加 -ness 构成，义为「荒凉；严酷」

entries.definition: with no clothes at all
entries.definitionCN: 固定搭配，义为「一丝不挂」

entries.definition: not covered or decorated
severe and unkind
complete and total

normalIntro.en: Stark keeps one idea through all its senses: something standing stiff and bare, with nothing soft around it.
normalIntro.cn: stark 的所有义项贯穿着一个想法：一样东西硬邦邦地立着，四周没有一点柔软之物。

normal.en: Stark contrast is the most common collocation in IELTS essays.
normal.cn: stark contrast 是雅思作文里最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Remember the fixed pair stark reality, and keep it apart from the estate word realty.
normal.cn: 记住固定搭配 stark reality，别和地产用语 realty 弄混。

normal.en: The adverb starkly is the form used in front of an adjective, as in starkly different.
normal.cn: 副词 starkly 放在形容词前用，如 starkly different。

normal.en: Starkers is British informal for stark naked and is never used in a formal essay.
normal.cn: starkers 是英式口语中「一丝不挂」的说法，正式作文里不能使用。

normal.en: Do not confuse stark with stack, which means a pile of things.
normal.cn: 不要把 stark 和 stack（一堆东西）弄混。

abstract.en: Picture a winter tree in front of a white wall, every leaf gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵冬天的树立在白墙前，叶子一片不剩。

abstract.en: See two swatches of black and white laid side by side, with no grey between.
abstract.cn: 想象两块纯黑和纯白的色卡并排放着，中间没有任何灰色。

abstract.en: Think of a frozen branch that snaps instead of bending.
abstract.cn: 想象一根冻硬的树枝一掰就断，不肯弯。

examples.en: The stark contrast between the two districts is obvious to any visitor.
examples.cn: 两个城区之间的鲜明对比，任何来访者都一眼能看出。

examples.en: Officials issued a stark warning about the coming storm.
examples.cn: 官员们对即将到来的风暴发出了严厉警告。

examples.en: The children were stark naked on the sand.
examples.cn: 孩子们光着身子在沙滩上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死打克」——死命打也会把人「剥光」，剩下赤裸的严酷现实；这只是谐音联想，词源上是古英语 stearc（僵硬）。

root: 古英语 stearc（僵直的、坚硬的）→ 中古英语 stark（光秃、朴素）→ 严酷、鲜明 → 加强语气（stark naked）；同源于 stiff 的僵硬概念族。

sensesIntro.en: Stark moves from a stiff surface to a bare surface, then to unsoftened facts, then to sharp contrast, and finally to plain emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: stark 从僵硬的表层移向光秃的表面，再到不加粉饰的事实，再到鲜明对比，最后成为纯语气加强。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frozen branch with no leaves, set against an empty sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根没有叶子的冻枝，衬着空荡荡的天。

branches.en: Bareness is the visible sense.
branches.cn: 光秃是可见的义项。

branches.en: Unsparing severity is the moral sense.
branches.cn: 严酷无情是道德层面的义项。

branches.en: Sharp contrast is the analytical sense used in writing.
branches.cn: 鲜明对比是写作中常用的分析义项。

branches.en: A bare scene and a clear contrast both lack middle tones.
branches.cn: 光秃的场景与鲜明的对比都缺少中间色调。

branches.en: Utter emphasis often appears in harsh warnings.
branches.cn: 十足的语气加强常出现在严厉的警告里。

intro.en: Stark is a Germanic root word with no prefixes of its own; English builds adverbs, nouns and slang forms on it with -ly, -ness and -ers.
intro.cn: stark 是日耳曼语中的根词，本身没有前缀；英语用 -ly、-ness 与 -ers 在它之上构成副词、名词和口语形式。

latinIntro.en: Stark has no Latin root; its Latin neighbours are only meaning borrowings such as rigidus for stiff and absolutus for absolute.
latinIntro.cn: stark 没有拉丁词根；它在拉丁语中的邻近词只是意义借用，如表示僵硬的 rigidus 和表示绝对的 absolutus。

items.example: Old English stearc supplies the hard core of the idea.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 stearc 提供这个词的坚硬内核。

items.meaningCN: 以……方式的名词转副词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ly forms starkly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 starkly。

items.example: Starkly different means very clearly different.
items.exampleCN: starkly different 意为差别非常明显。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms starkness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 starkness。

items.example: Starkness names the quality of being bare.
items.exampleCN: starkness 指光秃、荒凉的性质。

items.meaningCN: 表示戏谑或强调的口语词尾
items.example: The slang ending -ers forms starkers.
items.exampleCN: 口语词尾 -ers 构成 starkers。

items.example: Starkers is intimate for stark naked.
items.exampleCN: starkers 是 stark naked 的亲密说法。

items.meaning: used before a participle for emphasis
items.meaningCN: 置于分词前起加强语气作用的成分
items.example: The combining form stark- gives stark raving mad.
items.exampleCN: 组合成分 stark- 构成 stark raving mad。

definition_zh: 使惊吓；使吃惊；惊动
definition_en: to surprise someone suddenly, so that they jump or feel a quick shock
core_image: 背后突然一声脆响，人整个一颤，肩膀猛地提起来
scene: 同伴从树后突然冒出来，把正在读信的她猛地吓了一跳。Her friend leapt out from behind the tree and startled her as she read a letter.
sceneCN: 这里 startle 是「使惊吓」（第 1 个义项：突如其来的响动或身影让人骤然一颤）；句意：同伴从树后突然冒出来，把正在读信的她猛地吓了一跳。

pos.zh: 惊吓；惊动，仅见于少数词组

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转来的形容词，义为「受惊的」
由现在分词转来的形容词，义为「惊人的；令人吃惊的」
由 startling 加 -ly 构成，义为「惊人地」
由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「惊愕；惊吓」

senses.title: To make someone jump with fright
senses.definition: to surprise someone so suddenly that their body jerks or their heart quickens
senses.definitionCN: 突如其来地使某人受惊，以至于身体猛地一颤或心跳加快
senses.example: A loud bang startled everyone in the quiet library.
senses.exampleCN: 一声巨响把安静图书馆里的所有人都吓了一跳。
senses.why: A start is a sudden involuntary jump, and startle is the verb made from it, so the word is the jump itself.
senses.whyCN: start 是猛然一惊、身体不能自主地弹一下，startle 由它变来，所以这个词就是「那一跳」本身。

senses.title: To surprise and unsettle
senses.definition: to surprise someone strongly in a way that leaves them uneasy or off balance
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地使某人吃惊，令其不安或心神不定
senses.example: What startled me was his calm voice after such a shock.
senses.exampleCN: 让我吃惊的是，经历这么大的震动后他语气如此平静。
senses.why: The body jump fades into a mental jolt, so startle also names strong surprise that unsettles the mind.
senses.whyCN: 身体的一跳淡化为心里的猛地一震，于是 startle 也指让人心神不宁的强烈吃惊。

senses.title: To disturb or chase animals
senses.definition: to disturb an animal or person so that they suddenly move or flee
senses.definitionCN: 惊动动物或人，使其突然移动或逃走
senses.example: Walk softly so you do not startle the deer.
senses.exampleCN: 脚步放轻些，别惊动了鹿。
senses.why: Because a startled creature bolts, the verb is used when people want to drive animals out of hiding.
senses.whyCN: 受惊的动物会突然窜走，所以人们把动物从藏身处赶出来时也用这个动词。

senses.title: The startling as an adjective
senses.definition: when turned into the participle startling, it describes something that surprises greatly, often with a hint of alarm
senses.definitionCN: 变为分词形式 startling 时，形容某事物极其出人意料，常带一丝警醒意味
senses.example: The team made startling progress in a single month.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在一个月内取得了惊人的进展。
senses.why: A thing that startles loses its ordinary look, so starting results came to mean results worth a jump.
senses.whyCN: 能让人吓一跳的东西就不再显得平常，于是 startling results 指值得人猛地一怔的结果。

intro.en: Startle is a frequentative of the verb start, which meant to jump or move suddenly; adding -le made it to make someone jump.
intro.cn: startle 是动词 start（猛地一动、跳起）的反复体，加上 -le 后表示「使某人猛地一跳」。

items.en: The root verb stierten means to leap up or to move suddenly.
items.cn: 词根动词 stierten 意为跳起、猛然移动。

items.en: Starten means to jump, to leap, or to be suddenly disturbed.
items.cn: 中古英语 starten 意为跳、跃，或突然被触动。

items.en: The frequentative ending -le yields startle, meaning to cause a sudden jump.
items.cn: 加上反复体词尾 -le 形成 startle，表示「使……猛跳一下」。

items.en: Startle widens to mean to surprise or alarm anyone.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，startle 扩展为「使任何人吃惊、受惊」。

items.en: Psychology adopts it in phrases such as startle reaction, and the derivative startling describes shocking facts.
items.cn: 心理学把它用于 startle reaction 等术语，派生词 startling 则用来形容令人震惊的事实。

note.en: Startle shares a root and a jump with start, and stands near alarm, scare, and shock in the meaning field of being surprised.
note.cn: startle 与 start 同源、同指「猛跳」，在「受惊」义场中靠近 alarm、scare 与 shock。

entries.definition: to begin, or to move suddenly with a jump
entries.definitionCN: 开始，或猛地惊跳，startle 的动词词干

entries.definition: suddenly frightened by something unexpected
entries.definitionCN: 由过去分词转来，义为「受惊的」

entries.definition: very surprising
entries.definitionCN: 由现在分词转来，义为「惊人的」

entries.definition: to make someone feel frightened or worried
to frighten someone, often on purpose
entries.definitionCN: 惊吓；吓唬，常指有意为之

entries.definition: to surprise and upset someone strongly

normalIntro.en: Startle is start plus a small -le ending: the verb that makes another person do a sudden start.
normalIntro.cn: startle 就是 start 加上小小的 -le 词尾：让另一个人「猛一激灵」的那个动词。

normal.en: The -le ending in startle works like the one in sparkle and twinkle, turning one quick action into a repeating or causing one.
normal.cn: startle 里的 -le 与 sparkle、twinkle 中的一样，把一个快速动作变成反复或使役的形式。

normal.en: Remember the pair become startled and a startling fact, both built from the verb.
normal.cn: 记住成对的 be startled 与 a startling fact，两者都由这个动词构成。

normal.en: The scientific fixed phrases are startle reaction, startle response and startle reflex.
normal.cn: 科学领域的固定搭配是 startle reaction、startle response 和 startle reflex。

normal.en: You can startle a person or an animal, but a person typically gets or is startled.
normal.cn: 可以说 startle 某人或某动物，但人通常是用 get startled 或 be startled 的形式。

normal.en: The noun startlement exists but is rare, so the adjectival spellings are worth learning too.
normal.cn: 名词 startlement 确实存在但很少见，因此形容词形式也值得记住。

abstract.en: Picture a hand touching a cold door handle and jerking back.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手碰到冰凉的金属门把，猛地缩了回来。

abstract.en: See a cat that was sleeping in a sunlit window leap to its feet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只在阳光里的窗台上睡觉的猫猛地跳起来。

abstract.en: Think of a quiet classroom when a chair scrapes across the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的教室里突然传来椅子擦地的刺耳声。

examples.en: The sudden flash of light startled the birds into flight.
examples.cn: 突如其来的灯光把鸟群惊飞了。

examples.en: She was startled to find the office empty at noon.
examples.cn: 中午发现办公室空无一人，她吃了一惊。

examples.en: Film directors use sound to startle the audience.
examples.cn: 电影导演用声音来惊吓观众。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死打特」——忽然被人死命打了一下，整个人「特」地一激灵；这只是谐音联想，词源上是 start（猛跳）加反复体词尾 -le。

root: 古英语 stierten（跳起）→ 中古英语 starten（猛跳）→ 反复体 startle（使猛跳、使受惊）；词尾 -le 与 sparkle、twinkle 同类。

sensesIntro.en: Startle begins with the physical jump, passes into a mental jolt, serves for driving animals away, and ends as the adjective startling.
sensesIntro.cn: startle 从身体的一跳出发，过渡到心里的一震，又用于惊走动物，最后凝固为形容词 startling。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body jerking upright at a sudden sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：突如其来的响声让身体猛地一挺。

branches.en: The physical jump is the base sense.
branches.cn: 身体的一跳是基础义项。

branches.en: Mental surprise is the inner sense.
branches.cn: 心里的吃惊是内在义项。

branches.en: Driving animals off is the practical sense.
branches.cn: 惊动动物是实用义项。

branches.en: Startling facts produce the same jolt as a sudden noise.
branches.cn: 惊人的事实带来的震动与突然的响声相同。

branches.en: A frightened deer and a startled student both bolt without thinking.
branches.cn: 受惊的鹿与受惊的学生都会本能地窜开。

intro.en: Startle is a Germanic verb with no prefix; its endings -ed, -ing, -ment and -ing plus -ly carry the word family.
intro.cn: startle 是日耳曼语来源的无前缀动词，它的词族由 -ed、-ing、-ment 以及 -ing 加 -ly 承担。

latinIntro.en: Startle has no Latin root; its English relatives come from the same start, while Latin supplies only meaning twins such as perturbare for to disturb.
latinIntro.cn: startle 没有拉丁词根；它的英语同族都来自 start，拉丁语只提供意义相近的词，如表示扰乱之意的 perturbare。

items.example: Start supplies the jump behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: start 提供整个词族背后的「一跳」。

items.meaning: to do repeatedly, or to cause to do
items.example: The suffix -le turns start into startle.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -le 把 start 变成 startle。

items.meaning: to frighten with a sudden shock
items.example: Startle is the frequentative verb.
items.exampleCN: startle 是反复体动词。

items.meaning: past participle ending used as an adjective
items.meaningCN: 过去分词词尾，可转作形容词
items.example: The suffix -ed forms the adjective startled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成形容词 startled。

items.example: Startled describes a person or an animal.
items.exampleCN: startled 描述受到惊吓的人或动物。

items.meaning: present participle ending used as an adjective
items.meaningCN: 现在分词词尾，可转作形容词
items.example: The suffix -ing forms the adjective startling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成形容词 startling。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms startlingly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 startlingly。

items.meaningCN: 动作或结果状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ment forms the rare noun startlement.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成少见的 startlement。

items.example: The prefix re- makes a restarted noise, as in restarted.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 构成 restarted 一类说法，如响声再次开始。

latinEntries.example: Perturbare is a Latin meaning twin for the sense of alarm.
latinEntries.exampleCN: perturbare 是与「使惊慌」义项对应的拉丁语邻近词。

latinEntries.example: Pavor names the fright that a startle brings.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pavor 表示被吓了一跳带来的惊恐。

definition_zh: 贮藏；隐藏；存放；私藏；藏匿处
definition_en: to store something safely or secretly, often in a hidden place, until you need it
core_image: 把东西塞进树洞，用草叶盖住洞口
scene: 出发远足前，哥哥把几块巧克力和小刀塞进树洞里，再用草叶盖住。Before the hike, my brother stashed some chocolate and a knife inside a hollow tree and covered them with grass.
sceneCN: 这里 stash 是「藏起来存放」（第 1 个义项：把东西悄悄藏到某处备用）；句意：出发远足前，哥哥把几块巧克力和小刀塞进树洞里，再用草叶盖住。

derivatives.zh: stash 加 -er 构成，指藏东西的人
stash 加 -ing 构成动名词，指藏匿存放的行为
stash 加 -ed 用作形容词，指被藏好存放起来的

senses.title: To hide and store something away
senses.definition: to put something in a safe or secret place and keep it there until it is needed
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到安全或秘密的地方保留起来，等到需要时再用
senses.example: She stashed her savings under a floorboard.
senses.exampleCN: 她把积蓄藏在一块地板下面。
senses.why: The word is of uncertain origin but has long meant to conceal and set aside, so hiding and storing travel together.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来源不确定，但长期表示「藏匿并搁置」，所以藏与存总是同时发生。

senses.title: To put something carelessly out of sight
senses.definition: to put something somewhere quickly and without care, usually out of sight
senses.definitionCN: 随手、草率地把某物放进某处，通常是不见人的地方
senses.example: He stashed the letters in a desk drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信件随手塞进了书桌抽屉里。
senses.why: If hiding needs no ceremony, any quick act of shoving something away feeds the same core image.
senses.whyCN: 如果藏匿不必讲究，那么任何快速把东西塞开的动作，都是从同一核心意象延伸出来的。

senses.title: A hidden store or hiding place
senses.titleCN: 藏匿处；私藏的一批东西
senses.definition: a quantity of something kept hidden, or the secret place where it is kept
senses.definitionCN: 被藏起来的一批物品，或收藏它的秘密地点
senses.example: The thieves kept a stash of stolen watches in the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 小偷们在地下室里藏了一批偷来的手表。
senses.why: The noun names the result of the verb: whatever has been stashed, and the place that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 名词指动词的结果：凡是被 stash 的东西，以及存放它的地点。

intro.en: The origin of stash is uncertain; it appears in English in the late 1700s and may be an informal variant of stow.
intro.cn: stash 的词源不确定，十八世纪末才在英语中出现，普遍认为可能是 stow（堆放）的口语变体。

items.en: No secure source is recorded; the word may be a slang variant of stow or of a dialect form.
items.cn: 没有可靠的来源记录；一般认为可能是 stow 或某地方言的俚语变体。

items.en: Stash is first recorded as a verb meaning to hide or put away.
items.cn: stash 最早以动词身份出现，意为隐藏或收起。

items.en: It spreads through sailors and soldiers as talk of stashing money and supplies.
items.cn: 水手和士兵在谈论藏钱、藏补给时使它逐渐传开。

items.en: The noun stash names a hidden supply, especially of money or goods.
items.cn: 名词 stash 指私藏的物品，尤指金钱或货物。

items.en: Budgeting and gaming talk use stash for money set aside and for saved items.
items.cn: 在理财和游戏语境里，stash 用来指留着不动的钱和存起来的道具。

note.en: Stash sits beside its closer relatives store, hoard, and hide, and beside the look-alike slash and stake.
note.cn: stash 与近义的 store、hoard、hide 相邻，也容易和形近的 slash、stake 混淆。

entries.definition: to cut with a sweeping stroke
entries.definitionCN: 砍；划破；削减（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a pointed post, or a sum risked
entries.definitionCN: 木桩；赌注；股份（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to pack or put things away tidily
entries.definitionCN: 把东西装好、收好（一般认为与 stash 有渊源）

entries.definition: to keep something until it is needed
to keep a large amount secretly for yourself
to put something where it cannot be seen

normalIntro.en: Stash is a short, blunt word: the hand stuffs something away and covers it up.
normalIntro.cn: stash 是个短促有力的词：手把东西塞进去，再盖住。

normal.en: Stash away means to put something by for later.
normal.cn: stash away 指把东西收起来留待以后。

normal.en: A stash often holds money, food, or goods kept out of sight.
normal.cn: stash 常指藏起来的钱、食物或货物。

normal.en: Compare stow: to stow is to pack tidily, to stash is to hide.
normal.cn: 对比 stow：stow 是整齐收好，stash 是藏起来。

normal.en: Compare store: both mean keep, but stash usually adds secrecy.
normal.cn: 对比 store：两者都表示保存，stash 通常多一层秘密。

normal.en: The doubled s in stashes marks the regular third person form.
normal.cn: stashes 里的双写 s 标出规则的三单形式。

abstract.en: Picture someone slipping a wallet behind a loose brick.
abstract.cn: 想象有人把钱包塞进一块松动的砖头后面。

abstract.en: Imagine a squirrel moving nuts into a hollow tree.
abstract.cn: 想象一只松鼠把坚果搬进空树干里。

abstract.en: Think of a drawer that only the owner knows how to open.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只有主人知道怎么打开的抽屉。

examples.en: He stashed the cash in an old tin box under the sink.
examples.cn: 他把现金藏在水槽下面的一个旧铁盒里。

examples.en: The children stashed snacks in a cave for their adventure.
examples.cn: 孩子们为探险把零食藏在一个山洞里。

examples.en: Police found a stash of forged documents in the attic.
examples.cn: 警方在阁楼里发现了一批伪造的文件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死塌」——把东西死死塞到角落里，塌下来也盖住它；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 词源不确定：一般认为可能源于 stow（堆放）的俚语变体，十八世纪末首见于英语；核心义为「把东西藏好存起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Stash starts as the act of hiding and keeping something, extends to any careless shoving away, and ends as the hidden supply itself.
sensesIntro.cn: stash 先指把东西藏好存起来的动作，再泛指随手塞开，最后指被藏起来的那批东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand stuffing something into a hidden corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西塞进隐蔽的角落。

branches.en: Hiding and keeping is the central action sense.
branches.cn: 藏起来保存是核心动作义。

branches.en: Careless shoving away is a relaxed version of hiding.
branches.cn: 随手塞开是藏匿的松散版本。

branches.en: The noun names the stored goods themselves.
branches.cn: 名词指被存放的货物本身。

branches.en: To stash something is to create a stash of it.
branches.cn: 把东西藏起来，就等于创造了那批私藏。

branches.en: Quick shoving often leaves a messy hidden pile.
branches.cn: 随手乱塞常常留下一堆杂乱无章的私藏。

intro.en: Stash is a short English word of uncertain origin, with regular -s, -ed, and -ing forms built on it.
intro.cn: stash 是来源不确定的简短英语词，围绕它构成规则的 -s、-ed、-ing 形式。

latinIntro.en: Stash has no secure Latin ancestor; it is a native or borrowing of uncertain path into English.
latinIntro.cn: stash 没有可靠的拉丁语祖先，进入英语的路径并不确定。

items.example: Stash is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: stash 是基础动词。

items.example: The ending -es forms stashes.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -es 构成 stashes。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾
items.example: The ending -ed forms stashed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 stashed。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms stashing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 stashing。

items.example: The suffix -er forms stasher.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 stasher。

items.meaning: out of sight or in reserve
items.example: Away in stash away marks putting something aside.
items.exampleCN: stash away 中的 away 表示把东西收起来。

items.example: Stashes is the plural of the noun.
items.exampleCN: stashes 是名词的复数。

items.example: Stow is the likely older relative.
items.exampleCN: stow 是可能更早的相关词。

definition_zh: 静止的；固定的；不动的；不变的；常住一地的
definition_en: not moving and staying in the same place or position
core_image: 一辆车停在路边，一字不动，车轮上落了灰
scene: 红灯亮了，路边那辆自行车一字不动地停在白线后面，车轮上的灰也没被风掀起。The light turned red, and the bicycle by the road stood stationary behind the white line, its dusty wheels still in the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 stationary 是「静止不动的」（第 1 个义项：处在原处、不移动）；句意：红灯亮了，路边那辆自行车一字不动地停在白线后面。

pos.zh: 静止的；固定的；不动的；不变的

collocations.zh: 静止人口；人口不增不减

derivatives.zh: stationary 加 -ness 构成名词，指静止不动的状态
stationary 加 -ly 构成副词，指静止不动地
拉丁语 statio 的直接后代，指固定站立之处、站点

senses.title: Not moving
senses.definition: standing still and not moving from its place
senses.definitionCN: 停在原地、不移动的
senses.example: The car stayed stationary at the crossroads for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆车在十字路口停了十分钟没动。
senses.why: Latin station, a standing place, gives the image of something that keeps standing in the same spot.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 station 指站立之处，因此核心画面就是一直站在同一个点上。

senses.title: Fixed in place or position
senses.definition: attached or set to a place so that it cannot be moved
senses.definitionCN: 被装设或安放在某处，因而无法移动的
senses.example: The lab keeps a stationary camera to film the plants.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室用一台固定摄像头拍摄植物的生长。
senses.why: If a thing stands at one station, it is fastened there, not merely pausing.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西固定站在某一个位置，就说明它被安在那里，而不只是暂时停下。

senses.title: Not changing in amount or level
senses.definition: remaining at the same level or amount over time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内保持同一水平或数量
senses.example: The town has a stationary population of about nine thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇的人口一直稳定在九千左右。
senses.why: A standing figure is a figure that does not rise or fall, so the stillness sense moves from space to graphs.
senses.whyCN: 站住不动的数字就是不升不降的数字，于是「静止」从空间转移到图表上。

intro.en: Stationary comes from Latin statio, a standing place, and the verb stare, to stand.
intro.cn: stationary 来自拉丁语 statio（站立之处）与动词 stare（站立）。

items.en: Stare means to stand, and statio means a standing place or post.
items.cn: stare 意为站立，statio 意为站立之处或岗位。

items.en: The adjective stationary shows a French spelling before settling into English.
items.cn: 形容词词形带法语拼写痕迹，随后进入英语。

items.en: The word describes something fixed to one place, related to a soldier standing at his post.
items.cn: 这个词最早描述固守一处的状态，与士兵站岗有关。

items.en: Use extends to machines, signals, and objects that are standing still.
items.cn: 用法扩展到静止的机器、信号和物体。

items.en: Science and demography add expressions such as stationary wave and stationary population.
items.cn: 科学与人口学增添了「驻波」「静止人口」等固定说法。

note.en: Stationary is often confused with stationery, the paper goods, and is close to fixed and still in meaning.
note.cn: stationary 常与表示文具的 stationery 混淆，意义上也与 fixed、still 相邻。

entries.definition: paper, pens, and other writing materials
entries.definitionCN: 文具（与 stationary 拼写仅差一字母，但意思完全不同）

entries.definition: a place where a service or vehicle stops
a figure of a person or animal
entries.definitionCN: 雕像（同样来自「站立」之意）

entries.definition: not moving at all
attached in one position
completely without motion

normalIntro.en: Stationary says what it means: something standing at a station, staying put.
normalIntro.cn: stationary 本身就说明了含义：像站在站点一样待着不动。

normal.en: Station is the noun inside stationary, and a station is a place to stand still.
normal.cn: stationary 里藏着名词 station，而车站正是停下站立的地方。

normal.en: Remember the letter a in stationary, as in the a of stay.
normal.cn: 记住 stationary 里的 a，就像 stay（停留）里的 a。

normal.en: Stationery, the writing paper, keeps an e, as in envelope.
normal.cn: 表示文具的 stationery 保留 e，就像 envelope（信封）里的 e。

normal.en: Remain stationary is the most common verb phrase for it.
normal.cn: remain stationary 是它最常见的动词搭配。

normal.en: Statue shares the standing root, so a statue also stands still.
normal.cn: statue 共享「站立」词根，所以雕像也是一动不动地站着。

abstract.en: Picture a parked bicycle with dust settling on its wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆停着的自行车，车轮上落满了灰。

abstract.en: Imagine a soldier at his post who never takes a step.
abstract.cn: 想象一名站岗的士兵，一步也不挪。

abstract.en: Think of a flat line on a screen that neither rises nor falls.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一条既不上升也不下降的平直线。

examples.en: In this experiment the drum must stay stationary while the belt spins.
examples.cn: 在这个实验里，鼓必须保持不动，而皮带在转。

examples.en: A stationary storm dumped rain on the same valley for two days.
examples.cn: 一场停滞不前的暴风雨在同一片山谷下了两天雨。

examples.en: Wages have remained stationary for three years.
examples.cn: 工资已经三年没有变动了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死呆那里」——死守着一个地方不动，就是静止；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stare（站立）→ statio（站立之处、岗位）→ 拉丁语形容词形式 → 英语 stationary，核心义「站住不动」。

sensesIntro.en: Stationary begins with the physical image of standing still, extends to things fastened in place, and finally describes figures that stay unchanged.
sensesIntro.cn: stationary 从「站立不动」的身体意象出发，扩展到被固定住的东西，最后指保持不变的数值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vehicle standing still with dust on its wheels.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆静静停着的车，车轮上落了灰。

branches.en: Standing still is the basic physical sense.
branches.cn: 站立不动是最基本的物理义项。

branches.en: Being fastened in place is the fixed sense.
branches.cn: 被安放固定是「固定」义项。

branches.en: A flat curve on a graph carries the stillness into numbers.
branches.cn: 图表上的平直线把静止带到数字上。

branches.en: A fixed object is both unmoving and attached.
branches.cn: 固定物体既不动又被固定住。

branches.en: A rate that is fixed does not change over time.
branches.cn: 被固定住的比率就是随时间不变的比率。

intro.en: Stationary is built on the Latin stem station, standing place, with the English adjective ending -ary.
intro.cn: stationary 建立在拉丁语词干 station（站立之处）之上，加上英语形容词词尾 -ary。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare means to stand, and statio means a standing place; both feed stationary and station.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立，statio 意为站立之处，二者共同构成 stationary 与 station。

items.example: Stare is the root of standing still.
items.exampleCN: stare 是「站立不动」的根源。

items.example: Statio gives the stem of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: statio 提供形容词的词干。

items.meaning: a place to stop or stand
items.example: Station is the plain noun form.
items.exampleCN: station 是平实的名词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成表示关联的形容词。

items.example: Stationary keeps only the adjective sense.
items.exampleCN: stationary 只保留形容词义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms stationarily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 stationarily。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms stationariness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 stationariness。

items.example: Statue shares the standing root.
items.exampleCN: statue 共享「站立」词根。

definition_zh: 文具商；文具店主；书商
definition_en: a shopkeeper who sells paper, pens, envelopes, and other writing materials
core_image: 一位店主站在柜台后，把一叠纸和一支笔递给顾客
scene: 周四下午，街角那家小店的文具商站在柜台后，把一叠信封和一支钢笔递给顾客。On Thursday afternoon, the stationer at the small corner shop stood behind the counter and handed the customer a stack of envelopes and a fountain pen.
sceneCN: 这里 stationer 是「文具商」（第 1 个义项：以卖纸张、笔墨为业的店主）；句意：街角那家小店的文具商站在柜台后，把一叠信封和一支钢笔递给顾客。

collocations.zh: 出版业公会（伦敦老牌行会）

derivatives.zh: 由 stationer 加 -y 构成，指文具、信纸，即文具商所售之物
stationer 的复数，也用作行业名

senses.title: A shopkeeper selling writing materials
senses.definition: a person whose shop sells paper, pens, ink, envelopes, and similar items
senses.definitionCN: 开店出售纸张、钢笔、墨水、信封等物品的人
senses.example: Ask the stationer for a box of envelopes.
senses.exampleCN: 向文具商要一盒信封吧。
senses.why: The Latin word described a person with a fixed post; by medieval times the post belonged to a seller of writing goods.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原指站在固定摊位或岗位的人，到中世纪，这个岗位落到了卖书写用品的人身上。

senses.title: A shop that sells such goods
senses.definition: a shop that stocks paper and other writing materials for sale
senses.definitionCN: 售卖纸张及其他书写用品的店铺
senses.example: The stationer on the high street has closed.
senses.exampleCN: 主街上的那家文具店已经关门了。
senses.why: In British shops, the person and the place are often called by the same word, so stationer can also name the shop.
senses.whyCN: 在英式店铺说法里，人和店常用同一个词，因此 stationer 也可以指这家店。

senses.title: A member of the Stationers Company
senses.definition: a member of the London guild that once controlled printing and publishing
senses.definitionCN: 伦敦一家曾掌管印刷与出版的老牌行会的成员
senses.example: The Stationers Company kept a register of printed books.
senses.exampleCN: 出版业公会保存着印刷书籍的登记簿。
senses.why: The guild of stationers grew from selling paper into controlling what could be printed, so the word also names a publisher.
senses.whyCN: 文具商公会从卖纸起步，逐渐掌握印刷许可，因此这个词也指出版商或公会成员。

intro.en: Stationer comes from Medieval Latin stationarius, a person with a fixed post, through Old French stationier.
intro.cn: stationer 来自中世纪拉丁语 stationarius（有固定摊位的人），经古法语 stationier 进入英语。

items.en: Stare means to stand, and a stationarius held a fixed post or stall.
items.cn: stare 意为站立，stationarius 指有固定摊位或岗位的人。

items.en: University stationers sold and loaned manuscripts of set texts near a fixed spot.
items.cn: 大学里的文具商在固定位置出售和出租指定教材的手抄本。

items.en: Stationier names a shopkeeper who sells books and writing materials.
items.cn: stationier 指售卖书籍和书写用品的店主。

items.en: Stationer enters English for a bookseller or seller of paper and pens.
items.cn: stationer 进入英语，指书商或出售纸笔的人。

items.en: The Stationers Company is granted the right to control printing in London.
items.cn: 出版业公会获得掌管伦敦印刷业的权利。

items.en: Stationer settles into the everyday sense of a dealer in writing materials.
items.cn: stationer 固定为日常义：书写用品商人。

note.en: Stationer is easily confused with stationary and stationery, and is close in meaning to newsagent and bookseller.
note.cn: stationer 容易和 stationary、stationery 混淆，意义上与 newsagent、bookseller 相邻。

entries.definition: paper, pens, and other writing materials
entries.definitionCN: 文具（由 stationer 派生，指所售之物）

entries.definition: not moving
entries.definitionCN: 静止的（拼写相近但词义不同，源自「站立」）

entries.definition: a fixed place where something stops
a shopkeeper selling newspapers and magazines
a person or shop selling books
a person or firm that produces books

normalIntro.en: A stationer stands at a post: the same standing root that gives station and stationary.
normalIntro.cn: stationer 是站在固定摊位上的人，与 station、stationary 共享「站立」词根。

normal.en: Station plus -er gives stationer, a person at a fixed place.
normal.cn: station 加 -er 就是 stationer，指在固定位置上的人。

normal.en: Stationer keeps an e before the final r, stationery keeps the -y.
normal.cn: stationer 结尾 r 前有 e，而 stationery 保留 -y 结尾。

normal.en: Stationery is what a stationer sells.
normal.cn: stationery 就是 stationer 所卖的东西。

normal.en: In British English a stationer is also the shop itself.
normal.cn: 在英式英语里，stationer 也可以指那家文具店。

normal.en: The Stationers Company once ruled over printing in London.
normal.cn: 出版业公会曾掌管伦敦的印刷业。

abstract.en: Picture a man standing behind a counter stacked with paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在堆满纸张的柜台后面。

abstract.en: Imagine a fixed stall in front of a university gate selling ink.
abstract.cn: 想象大学门口一个固定的摊位在卖墨水。

abstract.en: Think of a guild hall where every printed book gets a stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一间公会大厅，每本印出的书都要盖章登记。

examples.en: The stationer recommended a cheaper brand of notepaper.
examples.cn: 这位文具商推荐了一种更便宜的信纸品牌。

examples.en: We buy our envelopes from a small stationer near the library.
examples.cn: 我们的信封是在图书馆附近一家小文具店买的。

examples.en: He worked as a stationer before joining the printing press.
examples.cn: 他在进入印刷厂之前做过文具商。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯泰神呢」——文具商在柜台后摆出一副斯文神态，递给你笔和纸；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stare（站立）→ stationarius（有固定摊位的人）→ 古法语 stationier → 中世纪英语 stationer，核心义「在固定摊位上卖书写用品的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Stationer begins as the person with a fixed stall, spreads to the shop that person runs, and ends as a member of the old guild of printers and publishers.
sensesIntro.cn: stationer 先指有固定摊位的人，再指此人经营的店铺，最后指老牌印刷出版公会的成员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seller standing behind a counter with paper and pens.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位售卖纸笔的人站在柜台后面。

branches.en: The shopkeeper selling writing goods is the central sense.
branches.cn: 卖书写用品的店主是核心义项。

branches.en: The shop itself takes the name of its keeper.
branches.cn: 店铺借用了店主的名号。

branches.en: Membership of a printing guild is the historical sense.
branches.cn: 印刷公会的成员身份是历史义项。

branches.en: A person and a shop are both called stationer in British use.
branches.cn: 在英式用法里，人和店都叫 stationer。

branches.en: The medieval seller of manuscripts grew into the printer and publisher.
branches.cn: 中世纪卖手抄本的人后来演变为印刷商和出版商。

intro.en: Stationer is the Latin word for a person at a fixed post, plus the English person ending -er.
intro.cn: stationer 源自表示「有固定摊位的人」的拉丁语词，并带有英语表人词尾 -er。

latinIntro.en: Latin statio means a standing place, and stationarius means a person who has a fixed post.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 statio 意为站立之处，stationarius 意为有固定摊位的人。

items.example: Stare is the distant root of the family.
items.exampleCN: stare 是这一词族的远祖词根。

items.example: Statio gives the word for a fixed place.
items.exampleCN: statio 给出表示固定地点的词。

items.meaning: a person with a fixed stall
items.example: Stationarius is the direct ancestor.
items.exampleCN: stationarius 是直接祖先词。

items.example: The suffix -er marks the person.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 标示出人的身份。

items.example: Stationer keeps the person sense.
items.exampleCN: stationer 保留指人的含义。

items.example: The suffix -y forms stationery.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 stationery。

items.example: Stationery names the goods.
items.exampleCN: stationery 指所售的货物。

items.example: The plural is stationers.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式是 stationers。

definition_zh: 文具；信纸信封等书写用品；办公用品
definition_en: paper, pens, envelopes and other materials used for writing or office work
core_image: 书店柜台上一摞信纸、一盒信封和一支钢笔并排放着
scene: 开学前，母亲带孩子去街角的文具店挑选笔记本和铅笔。Before the term began, the mother took her child to pick up notebooks and pencils at the local stationery shop.
sceneCN: 这里 stationery 是「文具」（第 1 个义项：供书写用的纸张与笔等用品）；句意：开学前，母亲带孩子去街角的文具店挑选笔记本和铅笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 stationery 去掉词尾构成的从业者名词，指「文具商；文具店店主」
stationer 的复数形式，指多家文具商或文具类店铺（常用于店名）

senses.title: Writing and office materials
senses.definition: pens, pencils, paper, notebooks and similar supplies used for writing or office work
senses.definitionCN: 供书写或办公使用的笔、纸、笔记本等用品
senses.example: The school provides basic stationery for every pupil.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为每个学生提供基本文具。
senses.why: The word began as the stock a bookseller kept for sale, and the goods on that stall became the materials themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指书商摊位上出售的货物，那些货物逐渐固化为书写材料本身。

senses.title: Paper for letters
senses.definition: decorated or good quality paper, with envelopes, used for writing letters
senses.definitionCN: 带装饰或纸质优良的纸，连同信封，用于写信
senses.example: She chose pale blue stationery for her thank you notes.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了淡蓝色的信纸来写感谢短笺。
senses.why: Because stationery once named the goods of a bookseller and papermaker, fine letter paper kept the word long after other supplies moved into general use.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词曾指书商与纸商的货物，精美信纸在其它用品普及之后仍保留了这个词。

senses.title: Shops that sell it
senses.titleCN: 文具；文具货源（店铺语境）
senses.definition: the range of writing goods stocked or sold by a shop, often in the phrase a stationery shop
senses.definitionCN: 商店进货或出售的书写类商品，常用于文具店这类说法
senses.example: Her family has run a stationery business since the war.
senses.exampleCN: 她家从战后就一直经营文具生意。
senses.why: The Latin root is a verb meaning to stand, an image of a stall that stayed fixed, so the word can still refer to the trade built on that counter.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「站立」，意象是一座固定不动的摊位，所以这个词也能指围绕柜台形成的生意。

senses.title: The goods distinguished from the seller
senses.titleCN: 文具用品（与文具商相对）
senses.definition: goods of this kind viewed as a mass, as opposed to the seller who deals in them
senses.definitionCN: 作为一种整体物品看待的此类商品，与出售它们的商家相对
senses.example: Prices for bulk stationery rose again this spring.
senses.exampleCN: 今年春天批量文具的价格又上涨了。
senses.why: The shorter spelling that dropped the final syllable came to mark the stock, while the longer form kept the person, a split that happens in many trade words.
senses.whyCN: 略去词尾音节的短拼写逐渐专指货物，而较长的形式保留指人，这种分化在贸易词汇里很常见。

senses.title: Materials held in stock
senses.definition: such supplies considered as stock held by a school, office or company
senses.definitionCN: 学校、办公室或公司持有的这类备货用品
senses.example: The office orders fresh stationery at the start of each quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室每个季度初都会采购新的文具。
senses.why: The medieval sense was a stock of books kept for sale, and the idea of held goods survives whenever supplies are counted and ordered.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的含义是备售的书籍库存，每当清点与订购用品时，这种「备货」的观念便延续下来。

senses.title: Printed cards and paper goods
senses.definition: printed cards, letterheads and other paper goods with printed designs
senses.definitionCN: 印有图案的卡片、信笺抬头等纸质品
senses.example: They printed wedding stationery in a small workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一间小作坊里印制婚礼用纸品。
senses.why: Paper and printing were the earliest goods sold at such a stall, so printed paper products remain the most typical reference.
senses.whyCN: 纸张与印刷是最早由这类摊位出售的货物，因此印制的纸质品始终是最典型的所指。

intro.en: Stationery hangs on the same root as station: a standing place, then a stall, then the books and paper kept on that stall.
intro.cn: stationery 与 station 同根：先有站立的场所，再有摊位，最后指摊位上备售的书籍和纸张。

items.en: Stare means to stand, and statio means a standing place or post.
items.cn: stare 意为站立，statio 意为站立的处所或岗位。

items.en: Estation carries the sense of a fixed position into French.
items.cn: estation 把固定位置的含义带入法语。

items.en: Stationarius names a seller licensed to keep stock at a fixed post, especially a book dealer at a university.
items.cn: stationarius 指获准在固定位置备货出售的人，尤指大学附近的书商。

items.en: Stationer appears for a bookseller, and stationery later marks the stock such a seller kept.
items.cn: stationer 先指书商，stationery 后指这类书商备售的货物。

items.en: Narrowed to writing materials, the word takes its usual spelling with an e near the end.
items.cn: 词义收窄为书写材料，并固定为词尾带 e 的拼写形式。

note.en: Stationery is a mass noun for writing supplies, easily confused with its homophone stationary, which means not moving.
note.cn: stationery 是表示书写用品的集合名词，很容易与同音的 stationary（静止的）混淆。

entries.definition: not moving, or not changing
entries.definitionCN: 静止的；不变的。只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同，与「文具」无关。

entries.definition: a place where trains stop or where a service is based
entries.definitionCN: 车站；站点，与 stationery 共享「站立之处」的词根。

entries.definition: a shopkeeper who sells paper and writing materials
entries.definitionCN: 文具商；文具店店主，由同一词根构成的人物名词。

entries.definition: food, equipment or materials that are needed for a particular purpose
entries.definitionCN: 补给品；用品，比 stationery 涵盖更广的物资。

entries.definition: paper, pens and ink used for writing
entries.definitionCN: 书写材料，是 stationery 的直白说法。

entries.definition: good quality paper for writing letters
entries.definitionCN: 信笺纸，对应 stationery 的信纸义项。

normalIntro.en: Stationery shares its root with station: a fixed counter where goods stand ready for sale.
normalIntro.cn: stationery 与 station 同根：货物摆在一个固定的柜台前待售。

normal.en: End the word with e, as in envelope, the paper goods it names.
normal.cn: 词尾是 e，就像 envelope（信封）一样，指的都是纸质用品。

normal.en: It is a mass noun, so we say a piece of stationery rather than a stationery.
normal.cn: 它是不可数名词，要说一件文具而不是直接加不定冠词。

normal.en: A stationer sells stationery, pairing the person with the goods.
normal.cn: stationer 卖 stationery，把人与其售卖的货物配成一对记。

normal.en: Compare stationary: the a form describes a parked car that does not move.
normal.cn: 对比 stationary：带 a 的那个词描述一辆停着不动的车。

normal.en: Office stationery covers paper, pens and envelopes ordered in bulk.
normal.cn: 办公文具包含成批订购的纸张、笔和信封。

abstract.en: Picture a shop counter with pens standing upright in a cup, waiting to be bought.
abstract.cn: 想象一个柜台，杯子里的笔直立着，等着被买走。

abstract.en: See a stack of cream letter paper beside matching envelopes.
abstract.cn: 看见一摞米色信纸放在与之相配的信封旁边。

abstract.en: Imagine the goods on the counter, not the person behind it.
abstract.cn: 把注意力放在柜台上的货物，而不是柜台后面的人。

examples.en: The company buys its stationery in large quantities.
examples.cn: 这家公司大批量采购文具。

examples.en: He left a note on monogrammed stationery.
examples.cn: 他用印有姓名首字母的信纸留了一张便条。

examples.en: There is a stationery shop on the corner of our street.
examples.cn: 我们街角有一家文具店。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「试占呢」——文具摊上先试笔再挑选；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stare（站立）→ statio（站立之处）→ 中世纪拉丁语 stationarius（固定摊位备货的持证商贩，尤指书商）→ 英语 stationer 与 stationery，核心义「固定柜台上备售的货」。

sensesIntro.en: Stationery starts with the stock held at a fixed stall, narrows to writing goods, and then widens to letter paper, printed cards and the trade itself.
sensesIntro.cn: stationery 从固定摊位上备售的货物出发，收窄为书写用品，再扩展到信纸、印制纸品和这门生意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fixed stall with paper and pens standing ready for sale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个固定的摊位，纸上和笔都摆好等着出售。

branches.en: Pens, paper and notebooks are the main everyday sense.
branches.cn: 笔、纸与笔记本是日常使用的主要义项。

branches.en: Fine paper for letters is the narrowed paper sense.
branches.cn: 写信用的精美纸张是收窄后的纸张义项。

branches.en: The trade built on the counter is the business sense.
branches.cn: 围绕柜台形成的生意是商业义项。

branches.en: The goods sense pairs with the person sense in everyday spelling habits.
branches.cn: 货物义项与人称义项在日常拼写习惯中形成对照。

branches.en: Stock kept for ordering and printed paper goods both keep the image of a stall.
branches.cn: 供订购的库存与印制的纸品都保留了摊位的意象。

intro.en: Stationery is built on the Latin stand root found in station, stationary and stationer.
intro.cn: stationery 建立在拉丁语「站立」词根之上，station、stationary 与 stationer 同出一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare means to stand, and statio means a standing place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立，statio 意为站立的处所。

items.example: Stare gives the standing image behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: stare 提供了整个词族背后「站立」的意象。

items.example: Statio develops into station in English.
items.exampleCN: statio 在英语中发展为 station。

items.example: The suffix -arius builds stationarius from statio.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -arius 由 statio 构成 stationarius。

items.meaning: a licensed seller at a fixed post
items.meaningCN: 固定摊位上的持证商贩
items.example: Stationarius first names a book dealer.
items.exampleCN: stationarius 最初指书商。

items.meaning: a place where something is based
items.example: Station keeps the fixed place sense.
items.exampleCN: station 保留了固定场所的含义。

items.meaning: a seller of paper and writing goods
items.example: Stationer keeps the person sense.
items.exampleCN: stationer 保留了人称含义。

items.example: The suffix -ery turns the person into the goods.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ery 把人称词转为货物词。

items.example: Stationary shares the letters but not the meaning.
items.exampleCN: stationary 字母相近，含义却不同。

items.example: Stationery is the goods kept for sale.
items.exampleCN: stationery 指备售的货物。

definition_zh: 立体声音响；立体声；立体声的；立体照片
definition_en: a machine that plays recorded sound through two speakers, or sound recorded in that way
core_image: 两只音箱一左一右，声音在房间里来回穿梭
scene: 客厅角落的老式音响放着旧唱片，声音从左右两只音箱里同时传出。An old stereo in the corner of the living room played a record, sending sound out of two speakers at once.
sceneCN: 这里 stereo 是「立体声音响」（第 1 个义项：带有两只音箱的放音设备）；句意：客厅角落的老式音响放着旧唱片，声音从左右两只音箱里同时传出。

pos.zh: 立体声音响；立体声；立体照片

derivatives.zh: 由 stereo 与希腊语声音词构成的形容词，指「立体声的」
由 stereo 加观看类词尾构成，指「立体视觉；立体成像术」
由 stereo 加观察仪器词尾构成，指「立体镜；立体视镜」

senses.title: A sound system with two speakers
senses.definition: a set of equipment with two speakers for playing recorded music or speech
senses.definitionCN: 带有两只音箱、用于播放录音的成套音响设备
senses.example: He turned up the stereo while cooking dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他一边做晚饭一边把音响调大声。
senses.why: Two channel sound caught on so quickly that the device itself took the short name of its sound.
senses.whyCN: 双声道声音普及极快，以至于设备本身直接用了这种声音的简称。

senses.title: Sound recorded on two channels
senses.definition: reproduction of sound through two channels so that it seems to come from different directions
senses.definitionCN: 通过两个声道重放声音，使人感到声音来自不同方向
senses.example: The album was remastered in stereo for the first time.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑第一次以立体声重制。
senses.why: The Greek element means solid, and two channels give the listener a solid, three dimensional image of the sound.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语成分意为「实体的」，两个声道让听者得到立体而有纵深的声像。

senses.title: The adjective use
senses.definition: using two separate channels of sound
senses.definitionCN: 使用两个独立声道的
senses.example: Her headphones offer stereo and mono modes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的耳机有立体声和单声道两种模式。
senses.why: Once the noun settled, the same short word was free to work as the adjective in front of sound terms.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法固定之后，同一个短词便可以直接放在声音类名词前充当形容词。

senses.title: Early stereoscopic pictures
senses.definition: a pair of photographs viewed together to give a single image with depth
senses.definitionCN: 两张照片配对观看，合成一幅有纵深的图像
senses.example: Her grandfather kept a box of stereos of distant cities.
senses.exampleCN: 她祖父保存着一盒远方城市的立体照片。
senses.why: The shorter word first named depth pictures, and only later was borrowed for depth sound.
senses.whyCN: 这个短词最初指有纵深感的照片，后来才被借用来指有纵深的声音。

senses.title: A short form in technical names
senses.definition: a short form of solid, used to make words about three dimensional depth or hard forms
senses.definitionCN: 意为「实体的」的缩写形式，用于构成表示三维纵深的复合词
senses.example: Stereochemistry studies how atoms are arranged in space.
senses.exampleCN: 立体化学研究原子在空间中的排列方式。
senses.why: Because it is a combining form first, stereo attaches to science words long before it names a radio.
senses.whyCN: 由于它本质上是构词成分，在指音响之前早已附着在各种科学术语上。

intro.en: Stereos is Greek for solid, and it was cut down to stereo from stereoscopic photography in the nineteenth century before it named sound equipment.
intro.cn: stereos 在希腊语中意为「实体的」，十九世纪它从立体摄影术语缩写为 stereo，之后才用于指声音设备。

items.en: Stereos means solid or hard, and stereon means a solid body.
items.cn: stereos 意为实体的、坚硬的，stereon 意为固体。

items.en: Stereoscope and stereoscopic are coined for viewing solid pictures from paired images.
items.cn: stereoscope 与 stereoscopic 被造出，用于通过成对图像观看立体画面。

items.en: Stereoscopic cedes its shortened form to stereo, first for depth photographs.
items.cn: stereoscopic 让位给缩写形式 stereo，最初指立体照片。

items.en: Stereophonic appears for two channel sound, modelled on the picture term.
items.cn: stereophonic 仿照图像术语出现，指双声道声音。

items.en: Stereos, meaning record players, becomes an everyday household word.
items.cn: 表示唱片机的 stereos 成为日常家居词汇。

note.en: Stereos, a solid, joins mono, one, and the depth word solid; stereo sound pairs with mono and surround.
note.cn: stereos 意为实体的，与意为「单一」的 mono 相对，也与 solid（实体）相邻；立体声常与单声道、环绕声并列。

entries.definition: a Greek adjective meaning solid, the source of the whole family
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语形容词，意为「实体的」，是整个词族的来源。

entries.definition: an instrument for viewing paired pictures in depth
entries.definitionCN: 用于观看成对图像而产生纵深的仪器，stereo 的缩写正由此而来。

entries.definition: a fixed idea that is applied to a whole group
entries.definitionCN: 固定化的成见，原指固定的铅版，与 stereo 共享「实体」词根。

entries.definition: single channel sound
entries.definitionCN: 单声道，与 stereo 相对的另一类声音方式。

entries.definition: a piece of equipment that sends out sound
entries.definitionCN: 音箱，是 stereo 系统的组成部分。

entries.definition: high fidelity sound equipment
entries.definitionCN: 高保真音响，与 stereo 常常一起出现。

normalIntro.en: Stereos means solid, so stereo sound is sound that becomes solid, with depth and direction.
normalIntro.cn: stereos 意为实体的，所以立体声就是变得立体、有纵深和方向感的声音。

normal.en: Mono has one channel; stereo has two, and the pair gives depth.
normal.cn: 单声道只有一路声音，立体声有两路，两路才产生纵深。

normal.en: The same stem sits in stereotype, once a solid printing plate.
normal.cn: 同一个词干出现在 stereotype 中，它原本指实心的铅版。

normal.en: Stereochemistry shows that stereo means depth in space.
normal.cn: 立体化学说明 stereo 表示空间中的深度。

normal.en: A stereo system is just the equipment that plays the stereo sound.
normal.cn: 立体声音响正是播放立体声的那套设备。

normal.en: Recorded sound in two directions is the core of the word.
normal.cn: 「声音从两个方向来」是这个单词的核心。

abstract.en: Imagine music arriving from the left and the right at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象音乐同时从左边和右边传来。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of photographs side by side becoming one deep scene.
abstract.cn: 想象两张并排的照片合成一个深邃的场景。

abstract.en: Think of a solid object you can walk around, not a flat drawing.
abstract.cn: 想起一件可以绕行的实体，而不是一幅平面图画。

examples.en: Turn the stereo down, the neighbours are asleep.
examples.cn: 把音响调小些，邻居们都睡了。

examples.en: The whole concert was recorded in stereo.
examples.cn: 整场音乐会都以立体声录制。

examples.en: Two stereos sat side by side in the shop window.
examples.cn: 橱窗里并排摆着两台立体声音响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死贴肉」——立体声贴着耳朵两边传来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 stereos（实体的、坚硬的）→ 十九世纪立体摄影术语 stereoscope 的缩写 stereo → 双声道术语 stereophonic 的简称 → 指播放这类声音的设备，核心义「实体感、纵深」。

sensesIntro.en: Stereo begins as a Greek word for solid, describes depth pictures, moves to two channel sound, and ends up naming the machine on the shelf.
sensesIntro.cn: stereo 起初是希腊语里表示「实体」的词，先描述有纵深的照片，再转向双声道声音，最后指架子上的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two speakers, left and right, filling a room with sound that has depth.
core.cn: 核心意象：左右两只音箱，把有纵深的声音填满房间。

branches.en: The household machine is the most familiar sense.
branches.cn: 家用机器是最为人熟知的义项。

branches.en: Two channel sound is the original sound sense.
branches.cn: 双声道声音是最早的声音义项。

branches.en: The adjective use places the meaning before nouns.
branches.cn: 形容词用法把这一含义放到名词之前。

branches.en: Depth photographs show the older picture sense.
branches.cn: 立体照片体现了较早的图像义项。

branches.en: Sound depth and science terms share the same solid image.
branches.cn: 声音的纵深与科学术语共享同一个「实体」意象。

intro.en: Stereos is a Greek combining form for solid, and English built stereo, stereophonic and stereoscope on it.
intro.cn: stereos 是希腊语中表示「实体」的构词成分，英语在其上构成 stereo、stereophonic 与 stereoscope。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; the element is Greek, so the same-root notes stay with the Greek source.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语祖先，成分来自希腊语，同源说明因此围绕希腊语来源展开。

items.example: Stereos supplies the solid image.
items.exampleCN: stereos 提供「实体」的意象。

items.example: Stereon shows the same solid idea as a noun.
items.exampleCN: stereon 以名词形式表达同样的实体概念。

items.example: The prefix stereo- begins the science words.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 stereo- 开启了一系列科学术语。

items.example: The looking element builds stereoscope.
items.exampleCN: 表示观看的成分构成了 stereoscope。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms stereoscopic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 stereoscopic。

items.example: The sound element forms stereophonic.
items.exampleCN: 表示声音的成分构成 stereophonic。

items.example: Stereoscopic is cut back to stereo.
items.exampleCN: stereoscopic 被截短为 stereo。

items.example: The single prefix mono- shows the opposite channel count.
items.exampleCN: 表示「单一」的前缀 mono- 体现了相反的声道数。

items.meaning: two channel sound or its equipment
items.example: Stereo is the everyday machine word.
items.exampleCN: stereo 是日常使用的设备词。

definition_zh: 立体的；立体视觉的；有纵深感的；立体显微镜的
definition_en: giving or using a three dimensional view of an object, usually from two slightly different images
core_image: 两张几乎相同的照片并排，合起来时画面忽然有了纵深
scene: 博物馆展厅里，孩子们戴上红蓝镜片，看完一面墙后忍不住惊叹画面仿佛要冲出纸面。At the museum, children put on tinted lenses and gasped as the images on the wall seemed to leap out of the paper in a stereoscopic display.
sceneCN: 这里 stereoscopic 是「立体的」（第 1 个义项：靠两幅略有差异的画面产生纵深）；句意：博物馆里，孩子们戴上彩色镜片，看到墙上立体展示的画面仿佛要冲出纸面，忍不住惊叹。

pos.zh: 立体的；立体视觉的；有纵深感

derivatives.zh: 由 stereo 与观看类成分构成，指「立体镜；立体视镜」
由同一词干加抽象名词词尾构成，指「立体视觉；立体成像术」
由 stereoscopic 加副词词尾构成，指「以立体方式地」

senses.title: Producing a view in depth
senses.definition: producing an impression of depth from two slightly different images seen at once
senses.definitionCN: 由同时观看两幅略有差异的图像产生纵深感
senses.example: The exhibition used stereoscopic images of the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 展览使用了老城的立体图像。
senses.why: Two eyes give two pictures of one scene, and the mind fuses the pair into depth, which is what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 双眼对同一场景得到两幅画面，大脑把这对画面融合出纵深，这正是这个词所描述的过程。

senses.title: Relating to binocular depth sight
senses.definition: connected with the kind of sight that judges depth by comparing two eyes
senses.definitionCN: 与依靠比较双眼来判断深度的视觉有关
senses.example: Failure of stereoscopic vision makes it hard to catch a ball.
senses.exampleCN: 立体视觉失效会让人难以接住球。
senses.why: The looking element marks this as a term about sight, so it names the animal or human ability as well as the picture.
senses.whyCN: 表示「观看」的成分表明这是一个关于视觉的术语，因此它既指图像，也指动物或人的观看能力。

senses.title: Viewing instruments
senses.titleCN: 立体仪器的；立体镜式的
senses.definition: used of instruments such as microscopes that show a solid object in relief
senses.definitionCN: 用于立体显微镜之类能呈现物体起伏的仪器
senses.example: Newly hatched insects were examined with a stereoscopic microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 新孵出的昆虫用立体显微镜观察。
senses.why: Laboratory practice joined the depth idea to the instrument word, so the adjective moved from the picture to the machine that makes one.
senses.whyCN: 实验室实践把纵深概念与仪器术语结合，这个词于是从画面转到制造画面的机器上。

senses.title: Mechanical stereo photography
senses.definition: of cameras that take paired pictures from two positions at the same distance apart as human eyes
senses.definitionCN: 指从相距约人眼间距的两个位置拍成对照片的摄影方式
senses.example: A stereoscopic camera took both cards in one click.
senses.exampleCN: 一台立体相机一次拍摄就得到两张照片。
senses.why: The device made for paired pictures was given the same adjective after the camera showed only one image, which is the ordinary case.
senses.whyCN: 专为成对照片设计的相机沿用了同一形容词，因为在普通摄影中相机只呈现一张画面。

senses.title: Figurative depth of description
senses.definition: giving a description that feels rounded and alive with depth
senses.definitionCN: 使描写显得圆融生动、富有纵深
senses.example: Her stereoscopic prose lets readers walk the streets with the narrator.
senses.exampleCN: 她立体化的文笔让读者与叙述者一同走上街头。
senses.why: Depth of sight is easily borrowed for depth of writing, so the adjective can praise a description that feels lived in.
senses.whyCN: 视觉上的纵深很容易被借来形容写作的纵深，于是这个词也可用来称赞身临其境的描写。

intro.en: Stereoscopic joins Greek stereos, solid, with skopein, to look, and was coined in nineteenth century science for paired pictures.
intro.cn: stereoscopic 由意为「实体」的希腊语 stereos 与意为「观看」的 skopein 合成，为十九世纪科学中成对图像而造。

items.en: Stereos means solid, and skopein means to look at or examine.
items.cn: stereos 意为实体的，skopein 意为观看、查察。

items.en: Stereometricus supplies a Latin adjective with the solid element before the compound appears.
items.cn: stereometricus 先提供一个带有实体成分的拉丁语形容词，复合词尚未出现。

items.en: Stereoscope is built for viewing paired pictures as one solid scene.
items.cn: stereoscope 被造出，用于把成对图像看成一个立体场景。

items.en: Stereoscopic is formed in French science and spreads with the craze for depth pictures.
items.cn: stereoscopic 在法语科学界形成，随立体照片热潮扩散。

items.en: The adjective is applied to microscopes, films and displays that show depth.
items.cn: 这个词被用于立体显微镜、电影与显示设备等呈现纵深的器具。

note.en: Stereoscopic is the long adjective of the stereo family, standing beside three dimensional and binocular.
note.cn: stereoscopic 是 stereo 词族中的长形容词，与三维、双目等同义场词相邻。

entries.definition: an instrument for viewing paired pictures in depth
entries.definitionCN: 用于观看成对图像的立体视镜，是 stereoscopic 直接描述的对象。

entries.definition: the technique or sense of seeing depth with two eyes
entries.definitionCN: 用双眼感知纵深的技术或能力，是其中的名词形式。

entries.definition: made of parts that slide into each other, or seen through a telescope
entries.definitionCN: 可伸缩的；望远镜的。只是词尾形式相近，词源不同，首个成分意为「远」。

entries.definition: having or appearing to have length, width and depth
entries.definitionCN: 三维的，是 stereoscopic 最直白的近义说法。

entries.definition: relating to seeing with both eyes together
entries.definitionCN: 双目的，强调两只眼睛同时参与，与立体视觉密切相关。

entries.definition: a depth image made of two coloured layers viewed through tinted lenses
entries.definitionCN: 用两色图层制成、透过彩色镜片观看的立体图像。

normalIntro.en: Break the word into a solid part, a looking part and an adjective ending, and the meaning is clear.
normalIntro.cn: 把这个词拆成「实体」成分、「观看」成分与形容词词尾，含义就清楚了。

normal.en: Stereos adds solid to skopein, to look, and the two make depth sight.
normal.cn: 表示「实体」的成分加上表示「观看」的成分，两者合成出纵深视觉。

normal.en: The scope is the tool; stereoscopic describes what the tool gives you.
normal.cn: scope 指工具，stereoscopic 描述这门工具带来的效果。

normal.en: Compare telescopic: that word looks far, this one looks deep.
normal.cn: 对比 telescopic：那个词看得远，这个词看得深。

normal.en: The heading of the pair of pictures is the same as the pair of eyes.
normal.cn: 一对照片的间距，与一对眼睛的间距是同一个道理。

normal.en: Stereoscopic vision is the animal sense; stereoscopic film is the made product.
normal.cn: 立体视觉是天生的感官，立体影像则是制作出来的产物。

abstract.en: Hold up your thumb and shut one eye, then the other, and watch it shift.
abstract.cn: 竖起拇指左右轮流闭眼，看它位置发生的偏移。

abstract.en: Imagine two slides moving together until the picture gains a back wall.
abstract.cn: 想象两张幻灯片慢慢重合，画面忽然多出一面后墙。

abstract.en: Think of a page whose figures lean toward you instead of lying flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上的图形向你倾斜，而不是平躺着。

examples.en: Owls lack a fully stereoscopic sense of sight.
examples.cn: 猫头鹰缺乏完全的立体视觉。

examples.en: The stereoscopic film made the crowd duck as a spear flew out.
examples.cn: 那部立体电影里长矛飞出时，观众纷纷低头闪躲。

examples.en: Engineers fitted a stereoscopic camera to the robot.
examples.cn: 工程师给机器人安装了一台立体相机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「实帖里死看」——两张照片实实地贴在一起，盯着看就有了立体感；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 stereos（实体的）+ skopein（观看）→ 十九世纪 stereo- 与 -scope、-scopic 合成的构词家族 → 英语 stereoscopic，核心义「观看时获得实体般的纵深」。

sensesIntro.en: Stereoscopic describes the picture, then the eyes that see it, then the instruments and cameras, and finally a depth of style in writing.
sensesIntro.cn: stereoscopic 先描述图像，再描述观看的眼睛，继而描述仪器与相机，最后扩展到文笔的纵深。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two nearly identical pictures sliding together until the scene stands out.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张几乎相同的图片合拢，场景立刻凸现出来。

branches.en: The depth picture is the defining sense.
branches.cn: 有纵深的图像是最核心的定义性义项。

branches.en: Two eyed sight is the biological sense.
branches.cn: 双眼视觉是生物学层面的义项。

branches.en: Microscopes and similar tools form the instrument sense.
branches.cn: 显微镜一类工具构成仪器义项。

branches.en: Paired lens cameras carry the word into photography.
branches.cn: 双镜头相机把词义带入摄影领域。

branches.en: A picture with depth and a sentence with depth share the same metaphor.
branches.cn: 有纵深的画面与有纵深的文字共用同一个隐喻。

intro.en: Stereoscopic is a three piece compound: a solid stem, a looking stem and an adjective ending, with stereo and stereoscope as relatives.
intro.cn: stereoscopic 是三分拼合的复合词：实体词干、观看词干与形容词词尾，stereo 与 stereoscope 是它的近亲。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word supplies this compound, but Latin stereometricus carries the solid element into early scientific English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词并不来自拉丁语，不过拉丁语 stereometricus 把「实体」成分带进了早期科学英语。

items.example: Stereos supplies the depth idea.
items.exampleCN: stereos 提供纵深的观念。

items.example: Skopein supplies the seeing element.
items.exampleCN: skopein 提供「观看」的成分。

items.example: The prefix stereo- opens the compound.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 stereo- 位于复合词开头。

items.example: The viewing element forms stereoscope.
items.exampleCN: 表示观看的成分构成 stereoscope。

items.example: The suffix -scopic forms stereoscopic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -scopic 构成 stereoscopic。

items.example: The suffix -ic makes the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 把词变为形容词。

items.example: The suffix -scopy forms stereoscopy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -scopy 构成 stereoscopy。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成副词形式。

items.example: The far prefix tele- builds telescopic.
items.exampleCN: 表示「远」的前缀 tele- 构成 telescopic。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to the measurement of solids

definition_zh: 无菌的；不能生育的；贫瘠的；枯燥无创造力的
definition_en: free from living germs; unable to produce young, crops, or new ideas
core_image: 一片被烈火烧过、什么也长不出来的田地
scene: 手术室的门上贴着一张告示，提醒每个人必须先洗手并戴上手套。A notice on the door of the operating room reminds everyone that the tools must stay sterile.
sceneCN: 这里 sterile 是「无菌的」（第 1 个义项：没有活菌、干净到可以消毒的程度）；句意：手术室门上的告示提醒大家，器械必须保持无菌。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 sterile 加 -ity 构成，义为「不育；无菌状态；贫瘠」
由 sterile 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「消毒；使绝育」
由 sterile 加 -ly 构成，义为「无菌地；无生气地」
由否定前缀 non- 加 sterile 构成，义为「非无菌的」

senses.title: Free from living germs
senses.definition: completely clean and free from bacteria or other living micro-organisms
senses.definitionCN: 完全洁净、没有细菌或其他活体微生物的
senses.example: The nurse opened a pack of sterile bandages.
senses.exampleCN: 护士拆开了一包无菌绷带。
senses.why: Latin sterilis means barren, so a sterile surface is one where no living thing can grow or survive.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sterilis 意为「不毛、不结果」，所以无菌的表面就是活物无法生长存活的地方。

senses.title: Unable to produce young
senses.definition: unable to have children or to produce offspring
senses.definitionCN: 无法生育子女或繁殖后代的
senses.example: The treatment may leave some patients sterile.
senses.exampleCN: 这种治疗可能使部分病人失去生育能力。
senses.why: The oldest sense of barrenness applies to living bodies that cannot create new life.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的「不结果」之义落在活体身上，就是一个无法孕育新生命的身体。

senses.title: Unable to grow crops
senses.definition: of land or plants, too poor or damaged to produce any growth
senses.definitionCN: 指土地或植物太贫瘠或受损，无法长出任何东西
senses.example: Years of drought left the fields sterile.
senses.exampleCN: 连年干旱让田地变得荒芜贫瘠。
senses.why: Barren land is the literal picture behind the word, so soil that yields nothing is called sterile.
senses.whyCN: 不毛之地正是这个词最字面的画面，什么也长不出的土壤就被称为 sterile。

senses.title: Lacking new ideas
senses.definition: lacking freshness, emotion, or creative power
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏新意、情感或创造力的
senses.example: The argument was sterile and solved nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 那场争论枯燥而空洞，什么问题也没解决。
senses.why: By metaphor, a mind or debate that produces nothing new is as barren as dry soil.
senses.whyCN: 用作比喻时，产不出新东西的头脑或辩论就像干裂的土地一样贫瘠。

intro.en: Sterile comes from Latin sterilis, meaning barren or unfruitful, probably from a root meaning stiff or dried up.
intro.cn: sterile 来自拉丁语 sterilis（不结果、不育），一般认为源自表示「僵硬、干枯」的词根。

items.en: A reconstructed root often glossed as stiff or barren may lie behind the word.
items.cn: 构词线索一般追溯到表示「僵硬、不毛」的重构词根，但具体形式存疑。

items.en: Sterilis describes land that will not bear crops and animals or people that cannot breed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sterilis 描述不长庄稼的土地，以及不能繁殖的动物或人。

items.en: The adjective enters English through Old French and Latin learning.
items.cn: 十四世纪中叶，这个词经古法语与拉丁学术用语进入英语。

items.en: Medical writers apply it to wounds and instruments kept free of infection.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪，医学作者用它形容不会感染的伤口与器具。

items.en: Modern science adds the sense of germ-free, and the word extends to barren discussion.
items.cn: 现代科学给它加上「无菌」之义，词义又延伸到毫无结果的讨论。

note.en: Sterile belongs to the Latin barren family and stands beside germ-free and fruitless words.
note.cn: sterile 属于拉丁语「不结果」词族，并与表示无菌、无成果的词相邻。

entries.definition: to make something free from germs
the state of being unable to produce
having no useful result
entries.definitionCN: 无效的；徒劳的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: unable to produce crops or young
free from infection or germs
producing good results or many young

normalIntro.en: Sterile is the image of ground where nothing can sprout, whether germs, babies, crops, or ideas.
normalIntro.cn: sterile 的画面是一块什么也长不出的地：不长细菌、不生儿育女、不长庄稼、也不长新点子。

normal.en: Sterile conditions in a lab keep samples clean and safe.
normal.cn: 实验室里的无菌条件让样本保持洁净安全。

normal.en: The verb sterilize is sterile plus -ize, meaning to make something germ-free.
normal.cn: 动词 sterilize 就是 sterile 加 -ize，意思是「使无菌」。

normal.en: The noun sterility names the state of being barren or germ-free.
normal.cn: 名词 sterility 表示不育或无菌的状态。

normal.en: Compare aseptic: both mean germ-free, but aseptic is the specialist medical term.
normal.cn: 对比 aseptic：两者都表示无菌，但 aseptic 更偏医学专业术语。

normal.en: A sterile debate is as useless as a field that yields no food.
normal.cn: 一场 sterile 的辩论，就像一块打不出粮食的田地一样没价值。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed dish on the lab bench where no germ can grow.
abstract.cn: 想象实验台上一个封死的培养皿，任何细菌都长不出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a tree that bears no fruit year after year.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵年年都不结果的树。

abstract.en: Think of cracked, dry earth under a cloudless sky.
abstract.cn: 想象无云天空下干裂的土地。

examples.en: All surgical instruments must be kept sterile.
examples.cn: 所有手术器械都必须保持无菌。

examples.en: The doctor warned that the drug could make her sterile.
examples.cn: 医生警告说这种药可能使她失去生育能力。

examples.en: The land around the old mine is sterile and dusty.
examples.cn: 那座旧矿场周围的土地贫瘠而多尘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死呆佬」——田里什么也不长，人呆立在荒地上；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sterilis（不结果、不育）→ 古法语 stérile → 英语 sterile，核心义「不结果实」。

sensesIntro.en: Sterile starts from barren land that yields nothing, and by extension nothing living, no children, and no new ideas grow there.
sensesIntro.cn: sterile 从「不毛之地」出发：不结果的田地产不出任何东西，引申开去就什么活物都不长、不生儿育女、也长不出新思想。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field burned dry where nothing can grow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被烧干、什么也长不出的田地。

branches.en: Where no living thing can grow, germs cannot survive either.
branches.cn: 任何活物都长不出的地方，细菌也无法存活，这就是无菌义。

branches.en: Barrenness applied to a body means the inability to have children.
branches.cn: 把「不结果」放在身体上，就是无法生养后代。

branches.en: Applied to soil, barren means land that will not bear crops.
branches.cn: 用在土壤上，「不结果」就是不长庄稼的贫瘠土地。

branches.en: Applied to speech or thought, barren means producing nothing new.
branches.cn: 用在言语和思想上，就是产不出新东西的枯燥无益。

branches.en: Both the germ-free sense and the poor-land sense keep the image of nothing growing.
branches.cn: 无菌义与贫瘠义都保留了「什么也长不出」这一核心画面。

intro.en: Sterile is a Latin-formed adjective; English builds sterilize, sterility, and sterilely around it.
intro.cn: sterile 是拉丁语来源的形容词，英语围绕它构成 sterilize、sterility 与 sterilely。

latinIntro.en: Latin sterilis means barren, and sterilitas names the state of being barren.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sterilis 意为「不毛的、不育的」，sterilitas 表示这种状态。

items.example: Sterilis gives the core image of barrenness.
items.exampleCN: sterilis 提供不毛的核心意象。

items.example: Sterilitas supplies the noun measure of the idea.
items.exampleCN: sterilitas 提供这一概念的名词形式。

items.example: Sterile keeps both the medical and the farming senses.
items.exampleCN: sterile 同时保留了医学义与农业义。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms sterility.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 sterility。

items.example: Sterility names the abstract condition.
items.exampleCN: sterility 表示抽象的状态。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms sterilize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 sterilize。

items.example: Sterilize is the action that creates the adjective.
items.exampleCN: sterilize 是制造这种性质的动作。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms sterilely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 sterilely。

items.example: The prefix non- forms non-sterile.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 non- 构成 non-sterile。

definition_zh: 消毒；灭菌；绝育；资金闲置
definition_en: the process of making something free from germs, or of making a living thing unable to reproduce
core_image: 一锅器械在沸水里冒着蒸汽，所有细菌被煮死
scene: 手术开始前，护士把所有剪子和钳子放进高压锅里高温处理。Before any operation, the nurse puts every scissors and clamp through sterilisation in a pressure cooker.
sceneCN: 这里 sterilisation 是「消毒、灭菌」（第 1 个义项：用高温或化学方法杀死所有细菌的过程）；句意：每次手术前，护士都会把剪刀和钳子放进高压锅进行灭菌。

derivatives.zh: 由名词 sterilisation 去掉 -ation 后缀构成的基础动词，义为「消毒；使绝育」
由动词加 -er 构成，指「消毒器、灭菌装置」
基础形容词，义为「无菌的；不能生育的」
过去分词转化而来的形容词，义为「已消毒的；已绝育的」

senses.title: Killing germs on equipment
senses.definition: the process of destroying all bacteria and other micro-organisms on objects or surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 用高温、化学药品等方法杀死物体或表面所有细菌及微生物的过程
senses.example: Proper sterilisation of needles prevents infection.
senses.exampleCN: 对针头进行适当消毒可以防止感染。
senses.why: Sterilisation is the noun of action built on sterile, so it names the process that makes a thing germ-free.
senses.whyCN: sterilisation 是由 sterile 构成的动作名词，因此指「使某物变得无菌」的过程。

senses.title: Cleaning water and food
senses.definition: the treatment of water, milk, or food so that it is safe to drink or eat
senses.definitionCN: 对水、牛奶或食品进行处理，使其可以安全饮用或食用
senses.example: Boiling is a simple form of water sterilisation.
senses.exampleCN: 煮沸是水质消毒的一种简单方式。
senses.why: The same germ-killing process is applied on a large scale to drinking water and food.
senses.whyCN: 同一种杀灭细菌的工艺被大规模用在饮用水和食物上。

senses.title: Making a person unable to reproduce
senses.definition: a medical operation that stops a person or animal from having offspring
senses.definitionCN: 使人或动物无法生育后代的医疗手术
senses.example: The animal shelter arranges sterilisation for every cat it takes in.
senses.exampleCN: 这家动物收容所会给每只收留的猫做绝育手术。
senses.why: The older sense of barrenness becomes a deliberate procedure that prevents new life.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「不育」之义变成一种有意为之的医疗程序，用来阻止新生命的产生。

senses.title: Keeping money idle
senses.definition: the business practice of holding money in a form that produces no return
senses.definitionCN: 企业把资金保存在不产生任何收益的形式中的做法
senses.example: Excess cash sterilisation can reduce the risk of inflation.
senses.exampleCN: 闲置多余资金有助于降低通胀风险。
senses.why: Unproductive money is as barren as dry soil, so economists borrow the word for idle funds.
senses.whyCN: 不能生利的钱就像不毛的土地，经济学家于是借用这个词形容闲置资金。

intro.en: Sterilisation is the noun of action from sterilise, formed from Latin sterilis, barren, with the suffix -ation.
intro.cn: sterilisation 是 sterilise 的动作名词，词根为拉丁语 sterilis（不毛、不育），加上后缀 -ation 构成。

items.en: The deeper root behind sterilis is uncertain, but it is generally linked to images of stiffness or barrenness.
items.cn: sterilis 更深的词根来源存疑，一般认为与「僵硬、不毛」的意象有关。

items.en: Sterilis means barren or unfruitful, and sterilitas names that state.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sterilis 意为不毛、不结果，sterilitas 表示这种状态。

items.en: French medical writing uses stérilisation for the removal of infection.
items.cn: 十八世纪法语医学文献用 stérilisation 表示去除感染。

items.en: English adopts the term as sterilisation during the rise of germ theory and surgery.
items.cn: 十九世纪细菌学说与外科手术兴起时，英语把该词吸收为 sterilisation。

items.en: The word spreads to water treatment, food science, and demography.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词扩展到水处理、食品科学与人口研究领域。

items.en: American English regularises the ending to sterilization, while British English keeps the s spelling.
items.cn: 美式英语把词尾规范为 sterilization，英式英语保留 s 拼写。

note.en: Sterilisation is the act noun behind sterile, close in form to sterilise and in meaning to disinfection.
note.cn: sterilisation 是 sterile 背后的动作名词，形式接近 sterilise，意义接近 disinfection。

entries.definition: to make something free from germs
a machine or substance that sterilises
the condition of being sterile
the removal of most germs from a surface
entries.definitionCN: 表面消毒；去除大部分病菌

entries.definition: heating milk or food to kill harmful germs
the state of being polluted by germs or chemicals

normalIntro.en: Sterilisation is sterile turned into an action noun: the whole process of making something unable to carry life.
normalIntro.cn: sterilisation 就是 sterile 变成了动作名词：一整套「让某物不再能承载生命」的过程。

normal.en: The suffix -ation turns the verb sterilise into the name of the process.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ation 把动词 sterilise 变成表示过程的名词。

normal.en: A steriliser is the machine that performs sterilisation.
normal.cn: steriliser 是执行 sterilisation 的机器。

normal.en: British spelling keeps the s, while American spelling uses a z.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留 s，美式拼写用 z。

normal.en: Compare disinfection: disinfection weakens most germs, sterilisation kills them all.
normal.cn: 对比 disinfection：消毒只是削弱大部分病菌，灭菌则把它们全部杀死。

normal.en: Medical sterilisation and the sterilisation of stray animals share one idea: no new life.
normal.cn: 医疗器械灭菌与流浪动物绝育共享一个概念：不再有新生命。

abstract.en: Picture steam rising from a sealed pot of surgical tools.
abstract.cn: 想象密闭锅里冒出的蒸汽，里面是外科器械。

abstract.en: Imagine clear water left in the sun until every germ is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象清水在太阳下晒到所有细菌消失。

abstract.en: Think of a bank vault holding cash that earns nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象银行金库里闲置、不生利息的现金。

examples.en: The hospital follows strict rules on the sterilisation of equipment.
examples.cn: 这家医院严格执行器械灭菌规定。

examples.en: Solar sterilisation can make drinking water much safer in remote villages.
examples.cn: 太阳能消毒能让偏远村庄的饮用水安全得多。

examples.en: The clinic offered free sterilisation for pets.
examples.cn: 这家诊所提供免费的宠物绝育服务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死呆里来婶」——呆在里屋的婶婶拼命用开水煮东西消毒；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sterilis（不毛、不育）→ 法语 stérilisation → 英语 sterilisation；sterile 加 -ation 表示「使其不毛」的整个过程。

sensesIntro.en: Sterilisation first names the process that kills germs, then treats water and food, then the medical removal of fertility, and finally idle money in finance.
sensesIntro.cn: sterilisation 先指杀死细菌的灭菌过程，再指水与食物的消毒，随后指让人或动物失去生育能力，最后指金融中的资金闲置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tools in boiling water where nothing can live.
core.cn: 核心意象：器械在沸水里翻滚，任何活物都活不下来。

branches.en: The core process of making an object germ-free is the medical sense.
branches.cn: 把物体变得无菌的核心过程就是医学上的灭菌。

branches.en: The same process protects drinking water and food.
branches.cn: 同样的过程被用来保护饮用水与食物。

branches.en: Preventing new life in a body is the surgical sense.
branches.cn: 在身体上阻止新生命产生，就是手术绝育。

branches.en: Money kept from producing returns borrows the barren image in finance.
branches.cn: 金融里不让资金生利，借用的是「不毛」这个画面。

branches.en: Both equipment and water sterilisation share the goal of a germ-free state.
branches.cn: 器械灭菌与水质消毒追求的都是一种无菌状态。

intro.en: Sterilisation combines the Latin base sterilis with the action suffix -ation, and English derives sterilise, steriliser, and sterile around it.
intro.cn: sterilisation 由拉丁词基 sterilis 与动作后缀 -ation 组合而成，英语围绕它构成 sterilise、steriliser 与 sterile。

latinIntro.en: Latin sterilis means barren, and sterilitas names the condition; the base travels through French into modern English nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sterilis 意为不毛，sterilitas 表示这种状态；这个词基经法语进入现代英语名词。

items.example: Sterilis supplies the root meaning.
items.exampleCN: sterilis 提供词根的「不毛」之义。

items.example: Sterilitas shows the noun pattern behind the word.
items.exampleCN: sterilitas 展示名词构成的模式。

items.example: Sterile is the base adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: sterile 是这一词族的基础形容词。

items.example: Sterilise adds the verb-forming -ise.
items.exampleCN: sterilise 加上构成动词的 -ise。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ation forms sterilisation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成本词。

items.example: Sterilisation names the whole process.
items.exampleCN: sterilisation 指整个灭菌过程。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 表示施动者或工具的后缀
items.example: The suffix -er forms steriliser.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 steriliser。

items.example: Steriliser is the machine of the process.
items.exampleCN: steriliser 是这个过程的机器。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms sterilised.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 sterilised。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 使不毛；使不育（中世纪拉丁语形式，一般认为）

definition_zh: 使窒息；闷住；抑制；扼杀
definition_en: to stop someone or something from breathing, moving, or developing freely
core_image: 厚厚的被子蒙住脸，喘不过气来
scene: 夏天的车厢挤满了人，空调坏了，窗户也关着。The heat and the crowd began to stifle everyone in the small bus.
sceneCN: 这里 stifle 是「使闷得喘不过气」（第 2 个义项：因闷热、拥挤而呼吸困难）；句意：闷热和拥挤开始让这辆小巴士里的人喘不过气来。

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转化而来，义为「令人窒息的；闷热的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「压制者」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「被压抑的」

senses.title: To stop the breath
senses.definition: to make it impossible for someone or something to breathe
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物无法呼吸
senses.example: Thick smoke filled the room and nearly stifled him.
senses.exampleCN: 浓烟灌满房间，几乎让他窒息。
senses.why: The verb is usually linked to Old French estouffer, to smother, and the original picture is a heavy cloth over the face.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一般认为来自古法语 estouffer（使窒息、闷死），最初的画面是一块厚布蒙住了脸。

senses.title: To feel unable to breathe
senses.definition: to be or feel short of air in hot or crowded conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在闷热或拥挤的环境中感到缺氧、呼吸困难
senses.example: She felt she was stifling in the crowded hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得在拥挤的大厅里闷得喘不过气。
senses.why: When the action happens inside the body, the verb turns into the experience of being smothered.
senses.whyCN: 当这种动作发生在身体内部时，动词就变成了「被闷住」的主观感受。

senses.title: To hold back a feeling
senses.definition: to keep a yawn, a laugh, or a cry from coming out
senses.definitionCN: 忍住哈欠、笑声或哭声，不让它发出来
senses.example: He stifled a laugh during the serious meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 在严肃的会议上，他强忍住笑。
senses.why: Like smothering a fire with a cloth, you cover a feeling so that it cannot get out.
senses.whyCN: 就像用布把火闷住一样，把一种情绪盖住，让它出不来。

senses.title: To prevent development
senses.definition: to stop something such as an idea, growth, or competition from developing freely
senses.definitionCN: 阻止思想、增长或竞争自由发展
senses.example: Too many rules can stifle creativity.
senses.exampleCN: 过多的规则会扼杀创造力。
senses.why: If a lack of air kills a fire, then blocking freedom of thought kills new ideas in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 缺氧会扑灭火，同样，束缚思想的自由就会以同样的方式扼杀新想法。

intro.en: Stifle comes from Old French estouffer, to smother, a word of uncertain deeper origin.
intro.cn: stifle 来自古法语 estouffer（闷死、使窒息），更深的来源尚不确定。

items.en: Some link the Old French word to a Vulgar Latin form related to stuff, but this is uncertain.
items.cn: 有说法把古法语词联系到与「塞满」相关的通俗拉丁形式，但这只是推测。

items.en: Estouffer means to smother or choke, used of covering the face or extinguishing a fire.
items.cn: estouffer 意为闷死、使窒息，用于蒙住脸或扑灭火。

items.en: Stiflen appears in English writing in this period.
items.cn: 十四世纪，stiflen 这一拼写出现在英语文献中。

items.en: The sense widens from physical choking to holding back feelings.
items.cn: 从十五到十六世纪，词义由身体的窒息扩展到压抑情绪。

items.en: Modern usage extends the word to any force that blocks freedom or growth.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到任何阻碍自由或发展的力量。

note.en: Stifle belongs to the smothering family and stands beside choke, suppress, and suffocate.
note.cn: stifle 属于「闷住」这一类词，与 choke、suppress、suffocate 相邻。

entries.definition: so hot or oppressive that it is hard to breathe
entries.definitionCN: 闷热得让人喘不过气的

entries.definition: a long gun fired from the shoulder
entries.definitionCN: 步枪（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: held back or choked
to die or cause to die from lack of air
to stop a feeling or activity by force
