to help something to grow or develop

normalIntro.en: Stifle is a cloth over the face: the breath is cut off, and the same image covers feelings and fresh ideas.
normalIntro.cn: stifle 就是蒙在脸上的一块布：呼吸被切断，这个画面同样用来盖住情绪和新想法。

normal.en: Stifle a yawn means to stop yourself from yawning aloud.
normal.cn: stifle a yawn 就是忍住不出声地打哈欠。

normal.en: Stifling air in a closed room is hot and hard to breathe.
normal.cn: 密闭房间里 stifling 的空气又闷热又难以呼吸。

normal.en: Compare suppress: suppress is more about authority, stifle more about air and flow.
normal.cn: 对比 suppress：suppress 更偏权威压制，stifle 更偏「不让空气或流动通过」。

normal.en: Heavy taxes can stifle small business growth.
normal.cn: 沉重的税负会抑制小企业增长。

normal.en: To smother a fire is to stifle it, leaving no air for the flame.
normal.cn: 闷住一堆火就是让它缺氧，火焰自然熄灭。

abstract.en: Picture a thick blanket pressed over a face.
abstract.cn: 想象一条厚毯子压在脸上。

abstract.en: Imagine sitting in a packed bus with no windows open.
abstract.cn: 想象坐在一扇窗都没开的拥挤巴士里。

abstract.en: Think of a lid clamped down on a box of fresh air.
abstract.cn: 想象一个盖子紧紧扣在一箱新鲜空气上。

examples.en: She tried to stifle a giggle when the speaker mispronounced the name.
examples.cn: 演讲者把名字念错时，她努力忍住笑。

examples.en: Heavy regulations may stifle innovation in young companies.
examples.cn: 繁重的规定可能会扼杀年轻公司的创新。

examples.en: The smoke was so thick that it began to stifle the trapped workers.
examples.cn: 烟太浓了，开始让被困的工人窒息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死提夫」——蒙在被子里死命提起力气，还是闷得喘不过气；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 estouffer（闷死、使窒息）→ 中古英语 stiflen → 现代英语 stifle，更深词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Stifle begins with the image of smothering: first cutting off air, then the feeling of it, then holding back a feeling, and finally killing anything that needs room to grow.
sensesIntro.cn: stifle 从「闷住」的画面开始：先切断空气，然后是这种窒息的感觉，再把情绪忍住，最后扼杀任何需要空间生长的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy cloth smothering the breath.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块厚布蒙住口鼻。

branches.en: Cutting off the air is the direct physical sense.
branches.cn: 直接切断空气就是最本义的身体窒息。

branches.en: The same smothering seen from inside becomes the feeling of gasping.
branches.cn: 从身体内部感受同一种闷住，就变成喘不过气的体验。

branches.en: Covering a feeling as if with a cloth is the sense of holding it back.
branches.cn: 像用布盖住一样盖住一种情绪，就是忍住的义项。

branches.en: Whatever needs air to grow dies when the air is blocked.
branches.cn: 任何需要空气才能生长的事物，一旦断了空气就会被扼杀。

branches.en: Both a stifled laugh and a stifled idea are things kept from getting out.
branches.cn: 被忍住的「笑声」与被扼杀的想法，都是被阻止「出来」的东西。

intro.en: Stifle is an Old French verb with few English affixes; its family is mainly built with -ing, -ed, and -er.
intro.cn: stifle 是来自古法语的动词，英语中几乎没有前缀，词族主要靠 -ing、-ed、-er 构成。

latinIntro.en: The word enters English from Old French estouffer; its Latin background is uncertain, so no firm Latin family is claimed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词从古法语 estouffer 进入英语，拉丁语背景不确定，因此不强行列出确定的拉丁同族。

items.example: Estouffer is the direct source of stifle.
items.exampleCN: estouffer 是 stifle 的直接来源。

items.example: Stifle keeps the smothering image.
items.exampleCN: stifle 保留「闷住」的意象。

items.example: The ending -le gives the word a repeated feel.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -le 让词带上反复动作的感觉。

items.meaning: smothers with he, she, or it
items.example: Stifles is the third person form.
items.exampleCN: stifles 是第三人称单数形式。

items.example: Stifled marks a completed action.
items.exampleCN: stifled 表示已完成的动作。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms stifling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 stifling。

items.example: Stifling describes oppressive air.
items.exampleCN: stifling 形容令人窒息的空气。

items.example: The suffix -er forms stifler.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 stifler。

definition_zh: 一阵工作；一段时间；限额；节省；克扣；吝惜
definition_en: a fixed period of work, or to limit and not give enough of something
core_image: 一把量得刚刚好的麦子，多一粒都不肯添
scene: 农忙时节，村里的短工只肯在地里干整整一个上午，天色一到就收工。When the summer harvest began, each hired hand did a single stint in the fields before the heat came.
sceneCN: 这里 stint 是「一阵工作、一段规定的活儿」（第 1 个义项：规定时长的工作）；句意：夏收开始时，每个短工在酷热来临前只在地里干了一阵活。

pos.zh: 一阵工作；一段时间；限额；配额

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「吝惜的；克扣的」
stint 加否定前缀 un- 与 -ing，义为「慷慨的；毫不吝惜的」
stint 加 -less，义为「无节制的；不知限额的」，多为文学用法

senses.title: A fixed period of work
senses.definition: a fixed amount of time spent doing a particular job
senses.definitionCN: 花在做某项特定工作上的一段固定时间
senses.example: She did a two-year stint as a village teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她当过两年乡村教师。
senses.why: Stint began as a noun for a limited allotment, so any job is seen as a measured portion of time.
senses.whyCN: stint 最初指「限定份额」，于是任何一份工作都被看成事先量好的一段时间。

senses.title: A limited share or amount
senses.definition: a limited amount of money or goods given as an allowance
senses.definitionCN: 作为配给或补贴发放的有限额度的钱款或物品
senses.example: The miners were paid a fixed stint of grain each month.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工们每月领到固定配额的粮食。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a portion measured out, the very same rationing image that still underlies the word.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「量出来的那一份」，至今仍是这个词的底层画面。

senses.title: To be sparing in giving
senses.definition: to give out or allow only a small amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 只给出或只允许很少量的某物
senses.example: The supervisor never stinted on safety equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 主管在安全设备上从不克扣。
senses.why: Once a portion is fixed, withholding part of it is a natural verb, so stint means giving too little.
senses.whyCN: 份额一旦被限定，扣下其中一部分就成了自然的动词用法，于是 stint 表示「给得太少」。

senses.title: Without any limit
senses.definition: used after without to mean generously and with no limit
senses.definitionCN: 用于 without 之后，表示慷慨大方、毫无限制
senses.example: The volunteers gave their time without stint.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者们毫不吝惜地付出了自己的时间。
senses.why: The phrase without stint reverses the idea of a fixed ration and points to a gift with no cap at all.
senses.whyCN: 短语 without stint 把「定额配给」反过来用，指一份完全没有上限的给予。

intro.en: Stint is first recorded in English in the thirteenth century with the sense of a limited amount, and the root is Old English styntan, to make blunt or short.
intro.cn: stint 在英语中于十三世纪最早出现，意思是「限定的数量」，其词根为古英语 styntan（弄钝、使缩短）。

items.en: Styntan means to make blunt or to cut short.
items.cn: 古英语 styntan 意为弄钝、使缩短。

items.en: The new noun first means a limited amount or allowance.
items.cn: 新生的名词最初指限定的数量或配给。

items.en: The verb develops the sense of limiting or being sparing.
items.cn: 动词逐渐发展出「限制、节省」的意思。

items.en: A stint of work means a fixed spell of duty.
items.cn: a stint of work 指一段固定班次的工作。

items.en: The word settles into a period of employment and the idea of being sparing.
items.cn: 这个词稳定为「一段任职时间」与「吝惜」两类含义。

note.en: Stint is nearest to stingy, stunted, and to ordinary words for periods of time and for being sparing.
note.cn: stint 与 stingy、stunted 拼写相近、含义相通，也和表示「一段时间」或「节省」的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: unwilling to give or spend
entries.definitionCN: 吝啬的；不肯给的，与 stint 的「克扣」含义相近

entries.definition: held back in growth
entries.definitionCN: 发育受阻的；长得矮小的，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: without any limit
entries.definitionCN: 无节制的；不知限额的，是本词的否定义派生词

entries.definition: a short period of a particular activity
a scheduled period of work
to use less than needed

normalIntro.en: Stint pictures a ration measured out: a job is a measured stretch of time, and giving is measured too.
normalIntro.cn: stint 的画面是「量出来的一份」：工作被量成一段时间，给予也被量得紧紧的。

normal.en: A stint is a measured period, so people do a short stint or a two-year stint in a post.
normal.cn: stint 是量好长度的一段时间，所以可以说 short stint 或「两年任期」。

normal.en: The noun also means a fixed allowance, the amount literally stinted out.
normal.cn: 名词也指固定配额，就是被量出来、限定住的那一份。

normal.en: To stint on something is to give too little, so never stint on safety.
normal.cn: stint on 某物就是给得太少，所以「在安全上不可吝惜」。

normal.en: Without stint is the opposite picture: giving with no cap at all.
normal.cn: without stint 是相反的画面：给予时完全不设上限。

normal.en: Compare stingy: stingy describes a person, stint describes the cutting down of a share.
normal.cn: 对比 stingy：stingy 形容人吝啬，stint 形容把一份份额削减下去。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer tapping a small cup of grain onto a scale and stopping at the line.
abstract.cn: 想象农民把一小杯麦子倒上天平，到刻度线就立刻停手。

abstract.en: Think of a sand timer flipped once: the job lasts exactly one glass.
abstract.cn: 想一只沙漏翻转一次：活儿正好做满一玻璃的时间。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand at a tap turning it off before the bucket is full.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在水桶快满之前就把水龙头关小。

examples.en: He spent a short stint working in a factory before university.
examples.cn: 上大学前他在工厂里工作过一小段时间。

examples.en: The coach never stints on praise for young players.
examples.cn: 教练从不吝惜对小球员的赞扬。

examples.en: Her stint as editor lasted only six months.
examples.cn: 她当编辑的时间只有半年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死盯」——死死盯住每一份量出来的东西，一份都不多给，就是「限额、克扣」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 styntan（弄钝、使缩短）→ 中古英语名词表示限定的数量或配给 → 引申为「一段固定的工作」「吝惜、克扣」，核心义「把东西量短、量少」。

sensesIntro.en: Stint starts from a measured share, grows into a fixed stretch of work, then into the verb of giving too little and the phrase for giving without limit.
sensesIntro.cn: stint 从「量出来的一份」出发，先长出「一段固定的工作」，再长出动词「给得太少」，最后有「毫不吝惜」的短语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small measure of grain stopped exactly at the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小份麦子正好停在刻度线上。

branches.en: A job becomes a measured stretch of time.
branches.cn: 工作被量成一段时间。

branches.en: The old ration sense survives as a fixed allowance.
branches.cn: 古老的配给义保留为固定配额。

branches.en: Holding back part of a share becomes the verb sense.
branches.cn: 扣下一部分份额就变成了动词义。

branches.en: The phrase without stint cancels the limit entirely.
branches.cn: 短语 without stint 把限额彻底取消。

branches.en: A stint of work and a stint of grain are both rations cut to size.
branches.cn: 一段工作与一份粮食同样都是被剪裁到固定大小的配额。

intro.en: Stint is a short native word with few affixes, but it builds a clear family through unstinting, stinting, and stintless.
intro.cn: stint 是简短的日耳曼本土词，本身词缀很少，但通过 unstinting、stinting、stintless 组成了一个清楚的词族。

latinIntro.en: Stint has no Latin root; it belongs to the Old English layer of the language.
latinIntro.cn: stint 没有拉丁词根，属于英语的古英语本土层。

items.example: A stint can name a job done for a set time.
items.exampleCN: stint 可以指做一段固定时间的工作。

items.example: The verb keeps the idea of cutting a share short.
items.exampleCN: 动词保留「把份额削减」的意思。

items.example: Both noun and verb take the form stints.
items.exampleCN: 名词与动词都取 stints 这一形式。

items.example: Stinted ends the past tense of the verb.
items.exampleCN: stinted 构成动词的过去式。

items.example: Stinting works as a verb form and as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: stinting 可作动词形式，也可作形容词。

items.example: The prefix un- negates stinting.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 使 stinting 变为否定。

items.example: Unstinting praise means praise given freely.
items.exampleCN: unstinting praise 指毫不吝惜的赞扬。

items.example: The suffix -less forms stintless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 stintless。

items.example: Stintless suggests giving with no cap.
items.exampleCN: stintless 表示给予时不设上限。

definition_zh: 规定；明确要求；约定
definition_en: to say clearly that something must be done, usually as a condition in an agreement
core_image: 合同里用一行字把条件一条条钉牢
scene: 签租约前，房东在纸上写明：退租必须提前一个月通知。Before the lease is signed, the landlord will stipulate that a month of notice is needed before leaving.
sceneCN: 这里 stipulate 是「明确规定、作为条件写进约定」（第 1 个义项：合同或条款里明文规定）；句意：租约签署之前，房东会明确规定，退租须提前一个月通知。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ation 构成，义为「规定；条款；约定」
过去分词作形容词，义为「规定的；约定的」
动词加 -or 构成，义为「订约人；提出条件者」

senses.title: To state as a condition
senses.definition: to state clearly that something is required as part of an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 明确说明某事是某项协议中必须满足的要求
senses.example: The contract stipulates that payment is due within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 合同规定付款须在一个月内完成。
senses.why: Latin stipulari meant to settle a bargain with a formal promise, so the modern word fixes a condition into the text.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 stipulari 意为以正式承诺敲定交易，因此现代词义就是把条件固定在文本里。

senses.title: To demand as a requirement
senses.definition: to demand something firmly and clearly from someone
senses.definitionCN: 坚决而清楚地向某人提出要求
senses.example: The rules stipulate a full week of training before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 规定要求考试前完成整整一周的培训。
senses.why: Once a condition is put in writing, it works as a firm demand on the other party.
senses.whyCN: 条件一旦被写下来，就变成对另一方不容含糊的要求。

senses.title: To agree on terms
senses.definition: to agree in advance on particular terms, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 事先就具体条款达成一致，多不带宾语
senses.example: Both sides stipulated for a fair price before the deal was sealed.
senses.exampleCN: 交易敲定之前，双方就合理价格达成了约定。
senses.why: The verb kept the everyday sense of the Latin bargain: you state and accept the terms together.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了拉丁语「谈买卖」的日常含义：双方一起把条件讲明并接受。

intro.en: Stipulate comes from Latin stipulari, to bargain or demand a promise, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: stipulate 来自拉丁语 stipulari（讨价还价、要求对方承诺），更深一层的来源尚不确定。

items.en: Stipulari means to bargain for a formal promise.
items.cn: 拉丁语 stipulari 意为为取得正式承诺而议定条件。

items.en: One doubtful account links it to stipula, a stalk of straw used in early bargains.
items.cn: 有一种存疑的说法把它联系到 stipula（草茎），古人讨价时用草茎折断作凭证。

items.en: Another traditional link is to stips, a small coin, but this too is uncertain.
items.cn: 另一传统说法联系到 stips（小铜币），同样无法确证。

items.en: The verb enters English as a legal term for arranging terms.
items.cn: 该动词于十六世纪进入英语，作为安排条款的法律用语。

items.en: Modern use broadens from legal bargains to any written condition.
items.cn: 现代用法从法律买卖扩展到任何成文条件。

note.en: Stipulate is close to stipulation, stipulated, and to ordinary verbs for saying what must be done.
note.cn: stipulate 与 stipulation、stipulated 同族，也与表示「要求、规定」的普通动词相邻。

entries.definition: a condition that is stated
fixed by agreement
a fixed regular payment
entries.definitionCN: 薪金；补助金，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to state something exactly
to need or demand something
to state what must be done by rule

normalIntro.en: Stipulate is the verb of the clause: someone names a condition and nails it into the agreement.
normalIntro.cn: stipulate 是「条款的动词」：有人提出一个条件，再把它钉进协议里。

normal.en: The pattern stipulate that is the most common, as in the contract stipulates that payment is due.
normal.cn: 最常见的是 stipulate that 句型，例如合同规定付款到期。

normal.en: Its noun is stipulation, a formal word for a stated condition in a deal.
normal.cn: 它的名词是 stipulation，正式指交易中写明的一项条件。

normal.en: As stipulated is a tidy phrase meaning as the agreement says.
normal.cn: as stipulated 是个简洁短语，表示「按规定、按约定」。

normal.en: Stipulate for is the intransitive use, meaning to bargain for terms.
normal.cn: stipulate for 是它的不及物用法，意为就条件讨价还价。

normal.en: Compare specify: specify names details, stipulate makes a detail a binding condition.
normal.cn: 对比 specify：specify 是说明细节，stipulate 则把细节变成有约束力的条件。

abstract.en: Picture a pen making a hard full stop after one short clause on a contract page.
abstract.cn: 想象在合同页的一个短条款之后，笔尖狠狠点上一个句号。

abstract.en: Imagine a stamp pressed onto a page to show a condition is now official.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章压在纸页上，表示条件已经正式生效。

abstract.en: Think of two people shaking hands and then writing down exactly what they promised.
abstract.cn: 想两个人握完手，再把彼此承诺的内容一字一句写下来。

examples.en: The lease stipulates that pets are not allowed.
examples.cn: 租约规定不得养宠物。

examples.en: Both parties stipulated a fair price before signing.
examples.cn: 双方在签字前讲定了合理的价格。

examples.en: The rules stipulate a minimum age of eighteen.
examples.cn: 规则明确规定最低年龄为十八岁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死定条款」——把条款一条条「死定」下来，就是「明文规定」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stipulari（讨价还价、要求正式承诺）→ 英语法律术语 stipulate（议定条款）→ 现代泛指「规定、明确要求」，核心义「把条件讲定并钉在约定里」。

sensesIntro.en: Stipulate moves from a written condition to a firm demand, and also keeps the older sense of agreeing on terms.
sensesIntro.cn: stipulate 从「写进协议的条件」扩展到「强硬要求」，同时保留了更早的「讲定条款」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clause nailed into a contract page and never allowed to move.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条条款被钉在合同页上，不得更改。

branches.en: The written clause is the central sense.
branches.cn: 写进协议的条款是核心义项。

branches.en: A clause also acts as a demand on the other side.
branches.cn: 条款同时是对另一方的要求。

branches.en: The Latin bargain survives in the intransitive sense.
branches.cn: 拉丁语「谈买卖」的含义保留在不及物用法中。

branches.en: People first bargain over terms, then write them as conditions.
branches.cn: 人们先就条款议价，再把条款写成条件。

branches.en: A stated condition is both a record and a command.
branches.cn: 写明条件的条款既是记录，也是命令。

intro.en: Stipulate is built on the Latin verb stem with the English endings -ate, -ation, and -or.
intro.cn: stipulate 建立在拉丁语动词词干上，并以 -ate、-ation、-or 等英语词尾构成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin stipulari, to bargain for a promise, is the direct source, with stipulatio as its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stipulari（议定承诺）是直接来源，其名词形式为 stipulatio。

items.example: Stipulari is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: stipulari 是整个词族的源头。

items.example: Stipulatio names the binding promise in Roman law.
items.exampleCN: stipulatio 在罗马法中指有约束力的承诺。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms stipulate from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把拉丁词干变成 stipulate。

items.example: The clause stipulates a clear deadline.
items.exampleCN: 该条款规定了明确的期限。

items.example: The stipulated sum must be paid on time.
items.exampleCN: 约定的款项必须按时支付。

items.meaning: the act of stating a condition
items.example: Stipulating terms protects both sides.
items.exampleCN: 订立条款能保护双方。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示行为的名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms stipulation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 stipulation。

items.example: Stipulation names the condition itself.
items.exampleCN: stipulation 指条件本身。

items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人的词尾
items.example: The suffix -or forms stipulator.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 stipulator。

items.example: A stipulator is a person who sets the terms.
items.exampleCN: stipulator 指提出条件的人。

definition_zh: 缝；缝纫；针脚；一针；缝合伤口；突然且剧烈的疼痛
definition_en: to join cloth or skin with needle and thread, or a single loop of thread in sewing, or a sharp sudden pain
core_image: 一根针带着线穿过布面，留下一个整齐的针脚
scene: 急救室里，医生把病人额头上的伤口缝好，一共刺了六针。In the emergency room the doctor decided to stitch the cut on her forehead.
sceneCN: 这里 stitch 是「缝合、缝上」（第 1 个义项：用针线把布料或伤口连接）；句意：在急诊室里，医生决定缝上她额头上的伤口。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 构成，义为「缝线；缝纫工作」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「缝纫者；订书机」
stitch 与 work 合成，义为「针线活」
back 与 stitch 合成，义为「回针缝」

senses.title: To sew with needle and thread
senses.definition: to join cloth or other material with needle and thread
senses.definitionCN: 用针线把布料或其他材料连接起来
senses.example: She stitched the hem of the old coat by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手缝好了旧外套的折边。
senses.why: The Old English verb stician means to pierce, so stitching is literally the needle going through the cloth.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 stician 意为「扎、刺」，所以缝就是在做针穿过布面这件事。

senses.title: To close a wound with thread
senses.definition: to join the edges of a cut in the skin with stitches
senses.definitionCN: 用缝线把皮肤上的伤口两边接合起来
senses.example: The doctor stitched the cut on his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 医生缝合了他膝盖上的伤口。
senses.why: Sewing and surgery share the same motion, so a wound is treated like a tear in cloth that must be closed.
senses.whyCN: 缝衣与外科用的是同一个动作，于是伤口被当成布料上必须收拢的裂口。

senses.title: A single loop of thread
senses.definition: one complete movement of a threaded needle through cloth
senses.definitionCN: 带线针在布上穿过一次的完整动作
senses.example: Every stitch on the jacket was even and neat.
senses.exampleCN: 夹克上的每一个针脚都匀称整齐。
senses.why: Each piercing leaves one loop of thread, so the noun names the single mark the needle leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 每刺一次就留下一道线圈，所以名词指的就是针穿过之后留下的那一个痕迹。

senses.title: A sharp sudden pain
senses.definition: a sudden sharp pain in the side or another part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 肋部或其他身体部位突然出现的一阵剧痛
senses.example: He felt a stitch in his side after the first lap.
senses.exampleCN: 第一圈跑完，他就感到肋部一阵刺痛。
senses.why: The pain is pictured as a needle pricking the body, turning the sewing image into an ache that stabs.
senses.whyCN: 这种痛被想象成一根针在扎身体，把缝纫画面变成了像针戳一样的疼。

intro.en: Stitch goes back to Old English stice and the verb stician, both meaning a prick or a piercing, and the older root is Germanic.
intro.cn: stitch 可追溯到古英语 stice 与动词 stician，二者都表示「刺、扎」，其词根是日耳曼语源的。

items.en: Cognates in Germanic languages all share a meaning of pricking or sticking.
items.cn: 日耳曼语各亲属语言中同源词的共同含义都是「刺、插」。

items.en: Stice is a prick or a puncture, and stician means to pierce.
items.cn: 古英语 stice 指刺、扎出的孔，stician 意为刺穿。

items.en: The noun comes to mean a loop of thread left by the needle.
items.cn: 名词逐渐指针穿过后留下的线圈。

items.en: The noun also names a sharp pain that feels like a prick.
items.cn: 该名词也开始指一种像被扎一下的突然剧痛。

items.en: Surgical stitching and expressions such as in stitches join the general uses.
items.cn: 外科缝合以及 in stitches 等说法加入其常见用法。

note.en: Stitch sits near the sewing words stitcher and stitching, and near ordinary words for sewing and for sharp pain.
note.cn: stitch 与 stitcher、stitching 等缝纫词相邻，也与表示「缝、刺痛」的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: the lines of thread on sewn cloth
a person or machine that stitches
needlework
entries.definitionCN: 针线活，是 stitch 与 work 的复合词

entries.definition: to join cloth with needle and thread
a stitch that closes a wound
a sudden slight pain

normalIntro.en: Stitch is always a needle going through something: cloth, skin, or the body in a flash of pain.
normalIntro.cn: stitch 的画面总是一根针穿过某样东西：布料、皮肤，或者一瞬间被扎痛的身体。

normal.en: As a verb, stitch means to sew, so people stitch a hem, stitch up a tear, or stitch a wound.
normal.cn: 作动词时 stitch 意为缝，所以可以缝折边、缝补裂口或缝合伤口。

normal.en: As a noun, a stitch is one loop of thread, and a row of stitches makes a seam.
normal.cn: 作名词时，一个 stitch 是一道线圈，一排针脚就形成一道缝。

normal.en: The saying a stitch in time saves nine means small repairs early prevent bigger trouble.
normal.cn: 谚语「a stitch in time saves nine」意为「及时一针省九针」，小修早做可免大麻烦。

normal.en: In knitting, to drop a stitch means to lose a loop and leave a hole.
normal.cn: 在编织中，drop a stitch 指漏织一针，留下一个洞。

normal.en: Compare sew: sew is the general act, stitch names the single piercing motion and its result.
normal.cn: 对比 sew：sew 是泛指缝纫，stitch 强调每一次穿刺动作及其痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a silver needle rising and falling through white cloth again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一根银针在白布上一起一落，反复穿过。

abstract.en: Think of a row of tiny loops like small links of a chain along a seam.
abstract.cn: 想缝线上一排小小的线圈，像一串小链环。

abstract.en: Imagine a quick jab in your side on the first lap of a race.
abstract.cn: 想象赛跑第一圈时侧肋被猛地刺了一下。

examples.en: He stitched the tear in his sleeve with black thread.
examples.cn: 他用黑线缝好了袖子上的裂口。

examples.en: Nurses stitched the wound in less than ten minutes.
examples.cn: 护士们在不到十分钟内缝合了伤口。

examples.en: She felt a stitch after running uphill.
examples.cn: 跑上坡之后，她感到肋部一阵刺痛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死贴」——针线一层层死死贴住布面，就是「缝、针脚」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 stician（刺、扎）与名词 stice（刺出的孔）→ 中古英语 → 英语 stitch，核心义「针一次次穿过而留下的痕迹」，由「刺」扩展为缝纫、缝合与刺痛。

sensesIntro.en: Stitch begins with the act of sewing, passes to closing a wound and to the single loop of thread, and ends with a pain that feels like a prick.
sensesIntro.cn: stitch 从「缝」的动作出发，先扩展为「缝合伤口」，再到「一针针脚」，最后指像针刺一样的剧痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle with thread passing through cloth and leaving a neat loop.
core.cn: 核心意象：带线的针穿过布面，留下一个整齐的线圈。

branches.en: The sewing action is the basic verb sense.
branches.cn: 缝纫动作是基本的动词义。

branches.en: Surgery borrows the same motion to close a wound.
branches.cn: 外科学借用同一动作来缝合伤口。

branches.en: The single loop of thread is the basic noun sense.
branches.cn: 单个线圈是基本的名词义。

branches.en: A pain is felt as a needle prick in the body.
branches.cn: 疼痛被感受为身体里的一记针刺。

branches.en: The act of sewing and the mark it leaves are two faces of one image.
branches.cn: 缝的动作和它留下的痕迹是同一个画面的两面。

intro.en: Stitch is a native Germanic word, but English builds a wide family around it with stitching, stitcher, and compounds such as cross stitch.
intro.cn: stitch 是日耳曼语源的本土词，英语围绕它以 -ing、-er 以及 cross stitch 等复合形式组成了丰富的词族。

latinIntro.en: Stitch has no Latin root; it comes from Old English and Germanic sources.
latinIntro.cn: stitch 没有拉丁词根，来自古英语与日耳曼语源。

items.example: Stice names the puncture the needle makes.
items.exampleCN: stice 指针扎出的孔。

items.example: Stician gives the piercing image of the word.
items.exampleCN: stician 提供这个词「穿刺」的画面。

items.example: The verb stitch covers sewing and surgery.
items.exampleCN: 动词 stitch 涵盖缝衣与外科缝合。

items.example: The doctor used four stitches to close the cut.
items.exampleCN: 医生用了四针来缝合伤口。

items.example: The badge was stitched onto the sleeve.
items.exampleCN: 徽章被缝在了袖子上。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms stitching.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 stitching。

items.meaning: the thread lines on sewn cloth
items.example: Stitching shows how the cloth was joined.
items.exampleCN: 缝线显示出布料是如何接合的。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms stitcher.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 stitcher。

items.example: A stitcher can also be a stapling machine.
items.exampleCN: stitcher 也可以指订书机。

items.meaning: a sewing pattern of X shapes
items.example: Cross stitch is a common compound with stitch.
items.exampleCN: cross stitch 是 stitch 常见的复合词。

definition_zh: 储备；存货；囤积；储备库；囤积起来
definition_en: a large supply of something kept in reserve for future use, or to collect such a supply
core_image: 仓库角落里越堆越高的一垛货物
scene: 冬天来临前，村里人把粮食一袋袋堆进谷仓，准备熬过漫长的雪季。Before winter, the villagers stockpile grain in the barn to survive the long snowy months.
sceneCN: 这里 stockpile 是「囤积、储备」（第 2 个义项：作为动词把物资大量积存起来）；句意：冬天来临前，村里人把粮食囤积在谷仓里，以熬过漫长的雪季。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「囤积；储备行为」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「囤积者；囤积的人」
复合词的前半部分，本身义为「存货；库存」

senses.title: A large reserve supply
senses.definition: a large amount of something kept in reserve for future need
senses.definitionCN: 为将来需要而大量积存的东西
senses.example: The country keeps a stockpile of emergency medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家保持着一批应急药品储备。
senses.why: Stock means a store of goods and pile means a heap, so a stockpile is a heap of goods set aside.
senses.whyCN: stock 指存货，pile 指一堆，两者合起来就是一垛被放在一边备用的货物。

senses.title: To accumulate for the future
senses.definition: to collect and keep large amounts of something for later use
senses.definitionCN: 大量收集并保存某物，供以后使用
senses.example: Some families stockpile canned food before a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 有些家庭在暴风雨来临前囤积罐头食品。
senses.why: The noun reserve became a verb, so to stockpile is to turn loose supplies into a standing heap.
senses.whyCN: 名词的「储备」义转成了动词，囤积就是把零散的物资堆成一座常备的货堆。

senses.title: A store of weapons or materials
senses.definition: a counted reserve of weapons, raw materials, or strategic goods
senses.definitionCN: 对武器、原材料或战略物资的清点过的储备
senses.example: Talks began to cut the nuclear stockpile.
senses.exampleCN: 削减核武器储备的谈判开始了。
senses.why: Governments keep an official count of what they store, so the heap turns into a measured national reserve.
senses.whyCN: 政府会对储存的物资做官方清点，于是那座货堆变成了可以计数的国家储备。

senses.title: A natural deposit
senses.definition: a natural mass of ore or mineral lying in the ground
senses.definitionCN: 地下自然形成的大量矿石或矿物
senses.example: Geologists mapped a rich stockpile of copper underground.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家绘制了地下丰富铜矿藏的分布图。
senses.why: The storing image is borrowed back to nature: the earth itself piles up metal in its depths.
senses.whyCN: 「囤积」的意象被借回自然界：大地自己把金属堆在深处。

senses.title: Hidden backup supports
senses.definition: a hidden supply of people or support kept ready for an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 为应急而备好、藏起来的人力或支援
senses.example: The campaign had a stockpile of volunteers waiting to help.
senses.exampleCN: 这场竞选活动有一批随时待命的志愿者后备力量。
senses.why: Even people can be piled up in reserve, so the word extends from goods to unseen human support.
senses.whyCN: 连人也可以被储备起来，于是这个词从物资扩展到看不见的人力支援。

intro.en: Stockpile is a compound of stock, an old Germanic store word, and pile, from Latin pila, a pillar or heap.
intro.cn: stockpile 由 stock（来源古老的日耳曼语「存货」）与 pile（来自拉丁语 pila，柱子、堆）复合而成。

items.en: Stocc names a tree trunk or stake, and later a store of goods.
items.cn: 古英语 stocc 指树干或木桩，后来引申为货物储备。

items.en: Pila means a pillar or a heap, and gives Latin pilare, to pile up.
items.cn: pila 意为柱子或一堆，并衍生出 pilare（堆起来）。

items.en: Pile enters English through Old French, meaning a heap.
items.cn: pile 经由古法语进入英语，意为「一堆」。

items.en: Stockpile is recorded as a noun for a reserve heap of goods.
items.cn: stockpile 作为名词首次见于记录，指成堆的备货。

items.en: In the twentieth century the verb stockpile spreads with military and crisis vocabulary.
items.cn: 二十世纪，动词 stockpile 随军事与危机类词汇一起普及。

note.en: Stockpile sits beside the stock family and beside ordinary words for stored supplies.
note.cn: stockpile 与 stock 一族相邻，也和表示「储备」的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: a supply of goods available for sale or use
a heap of things lying one on another
an enclosure where livestock are kept before sale
a secret store of money or goods
a supply kept for later use
an amount of something available

normalIntro.en: Stockpile is simply a stock plus a pile: goods kept in a heap against the day you need them.
normalIntro.cn: stockpile 就是 stock 加 pile：把存货堆成一垛，等着缺货那天再取。

normal.en: Stock means a supply and pile means a heap, so stockpile is a heap of supplies.
normal.cn: stock 是存货，pile 是一堆，所以 stockpile 就是一堆存货。

normal.en: A stockpile of food keeps a household safe through a hard winter.
normal.cn: 粮食储备让一家人在严冬中安然无恙。

normal.en: To stockpile is the verb: families stockpile food before a storm.
normal.cn: stockpile 作动词，表示在暴风雨前囤积食物。

normal.en: Build up a stockpile means to make the heap taller on purpose.
normal.cn: build up a stockpile 就是故意把那垛货堆得更高。

normal.en: Compare hoard: hoarding is secret and greedy, stockpiling can be practical planning.
normal.cn: 对比 hoard：hoard 偷偷摸摸又贪心，stockpile 则可以是务实的规划。

abstract.en: Picture a barn corner where sacks keep climbing upward day after day.
abstract.cn: 想象谷仓一角，粮袋一天天往上堆高。

abstract.en: Imagine a family packing tins into a cellar shelf before a storm.
abstract.cn: 想象暴风雨来临前，一家人把罐头码上地窖的架子。

abstract.en: Think of a whiteboard where tanks and missiles are counted in columns.
abstract.cn: 想象一块白板，坦克和导弹在一栏一栏地被计数。

examples.en: The hospital maintains a stockpile of masks and gloves.
examples.cn: 医院保持着一批口罩和手套储备。

examples.en: Some shoppers stockpiled rice when prices rose.
examples.cn: 米价上涨时，一些顾客囤积了大米。

examples.en: Nations agreed to reduce their stockpiles of chemical weapons.
examples.cn: 各国同意削减化学武器储备。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死多克派欧」——货堆得死多，派个欧也要守着，就是「囤积」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 stocc（树干、木桩，后引申为货物储备）+ 古法语 pile（来自拉丁语 pila，柱子、一堆）→ stockpile，核心义「成堆存放的备用物资」。

sensesIntro.en: Stockpile starts from a heap of goods set aside, turns into the act of collecting, and then broadens to military reserves, natural deposits, and hidden human support.
sensesIntro.cn: stockpile 从「堆放起来备用的货」出发，转为囤积这一动作，再扩展到军备储备、自然矿藏与隐藏的人力后援。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap of goods set aside in a warehouse corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：仓库一角堆放起来的备用货物。

branches.en: A reserve supply is the everyday noun sense.
branches.cn: 储备物资是最日常的名词义项。

branches.en: The noun turned verb means to build up that reserve.
branches.cn: 名词转动词，表示把这份储备慢慢堆起来。

branches.en: Weapons and materials give the counted official sense.
branches.cn: 武器与物资构成了可计数的官方储备义项。

branches.en: Both a barn reserve and a mineral deposit are masses lying in wait.
branches.cn: 谷仓储备与地下矿藏都是静静躺在那里的一团物质。

branches.en: Collecting people as backup is stockpiling in a human sense.
branches.cn: 把人备起来当后援，就是人这一层面的囤积。

intro.en: Stockpile is a native compound of the stock family and the pile family, with a small cluster of modern derivatives.
intro.cn: stockpile 是 stock 一族与 pile 一族复合而成的英语词，并围绕它产生了少量现代派生词。

latinIntro.en: Only the pile half has a Latin source: Latin pila, a pillar or heap.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 pile 这一半有拉丁语来源：拉丁语 pila，意为柱子或一堆。

items.example: Stocc gives the first half of the word.
items.exampleCN: stocc 提供了这个词的前半部分。

items.example: Stock is the base noun of the compound.
items.exampleCN: stock 是复合词的基础名词。

items.example: Pila lies behind the second half.
items.exampleCN: pila 是后半部分的来源。

items.example: Pile supplies the heap image.
items.exampleCN: pile 提供「一堆」的意象。

items.example: Stockpile joins both halves.
items.exampleCN: stockpile 把两部分合在一起。

items.example: The plural marks several reserves.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式表示多处储备。

items.example: The past form reports the act.
items.exampleCN: 过去式陈述囤积这一动作。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms stockpiling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 stockpiling。

items.example: The suffix -er forms stockpiler.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 stockpiler。

definition_zh: 矮壮的；结实的；（物体）粗短的；矮壮的人
definition_en: short and strongly built, with a thick, solid body
core_image: 一堵短而厚的石墙，稳稳立在原地
scene: 那位老摔跤手不高，但肩膀宽厚，站在场边像一段粗黄的树桩。The old wrestler was not tall, but his shoulders were wide and his stocky build looked impossible to push over.
sceneCN: 这里 stocky 是「矮壮的」（第 1 个义项：身材矮而结实）；句意：那位老摔跤手个子不高，但肩膀很宽，他那矮壮的身板看起来谁都推不倒。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「矮壮；粗壮」
形容词加 -ily 构成，义为「矮壮地；粗壮地」
同源基础名词，原义「树干、木桩」，引申为「存货」

senses.title: Short and strongly built
senses.definition: having a short, thick body that looks strong and solid
senses.definitionCN: 身材矮而粗厚，看起来强壮结实
senses.example: A stocky woman lifted the crate with ease.
senses.exampleCN: 一位矮壮的女人轻松地搬起了那只木箱。
senses.why: The word comes from stock, a tree trunk, so a stocky person has the short thick strength of a stump.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 stock（树干、木桩），所以 stocky 的人带有树桩那种矮而粗壮的力气感。

senses.title: Thick and short in shape
senses.definition: short and thick in form, used of limbs, tools, or plants
senses.definitionCN: 外形又短又粗，多用于肢体、器具或植物
senses.example: The old lamp had a stocky brass base.
senses.exampleCN: 那盏旧台灯有一个粗短的黄铜底座。
senses.why: Once the trunk image leaves the human body, any short thick object can be called stocky.
senses.whyCN: 树桩意象一旦离开人体，任何又短又粗的物体都可以叫 stocky。

senses.title: Forceful and direct in manner
senses.titleCN: 劲儿十足的；直来直去的
senses.definition: describing speech or action that is short, blunt, and forceful
senses.definitionCN: 形容话语或行动简短、直接、有劲
senses.example: His stocky sentences left no room for argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他那直截了当的句子不容反驳。
senses.why: The solid body image extends to style, so short blunt words feel stocky too.
senses.whyCN: 结实的身形意象延伸到风格上，于是简短有力的话语也显得「矮壮」。

senses.title: A short powerful person
senses.definition: a colloquial noun for a short, strongly built person
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来称呼身材矮而结实的人
senses.example: The stockies on the team did all the heavy lifting.
senses.exampleCN: 队里的矮壮汉子们承担了所有重活。
senses.why: The adjective is used as a noun, so the quality stands for the person who has it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词被当作名词使用，于是「矮壮」这一特质就代表了具备它的人。

intro.en: Stocky is formed from stock, an old Germanic word for a tree trunk, plus the adjectival ending -y.
intro.cn: stocky 由 stock（古老的日耳曼语词，指树干）加形容词词尾 -y 构成。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning a trunk or stake lies behind stock.
items.cn: 一个意为树干或木桩的日耳曼语重构词根是 stock 的来源。

items.en: Stocc means a trunk or post, joining by analogy to a store of goods.
items.cn: 古英语 stocc 指树干或立柱，又经类推引申为货物储备。

items.en: Stock also names the wooden block or the sum of money put into trade.
items.cn: 中古英语中 stock 又指木墩，也指投入生意的资金。

items.en: The adjective stocky is recorded for a thickset body.
items.cn: 形容词 stocky 首次见于记录，指粗壮敦实的身躯。

items.en: Modern English extends stocky to limbs, plants, and compact objects.
items.cn: 现代英语把 stocky 扩展到四肢、植物和紧凑的物件。

note.en: Stocky belongs to the stock family of trunk words and sits beside other words for body shape.
note.cn: stocky 属于表示「树干」的 stock 一族，并与描述体型的一批词相邻。

entries.definition: a trunk, a store of goods, or company shares
rather fat or solid, sometimes simply strong
entries.definitionCN: 有些胖而结实的，有时只指强壮，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the past form of stick
entries.definitionCN: stick 的过去式，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: large and solid in body
big and strong, often tall too
firmly built and hard to damage

normalIntro.en: Stocky hides the word stock inside it: a short thick tree trunk, not a tall thin one.
normalIntro.cn: stocky 里藏着 stock：它说的是又矮又粗的树桩，而不是细高的树干。

normal.en: Stocky comes from stock, a tree trunk, so the build is trunk-like: short and thick.
normal.cn: stocky 来自 stock（树干），所以这种身材像树干：矮而粗。

normal.en: A stocky build is praised for strength more than height.
normal.cn: stocky build 赞的是力量，而不是身高。

normal.en: The -y ending turns the noun stock into a descriptive adjective.
normal.cn: 词尾 -y 把名词 stock 变成描写性的形容词。

normal.en: Use the suffix -ness to name the quality: stockiness.
normal.cn: 用词尾 -ness 称呼这种特质：stockiness。

normal.en: Compare thickset and burly: stocky stresses shortness, burly allows height.
normal.cn: 对比 thickset 和 burly：stocky 强调矮，burly 则允许高。

abstract.en: Picture a low, thick stone wall holding firm in wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵又低又厚的石墙在风里纹丝不动。

abstract.en: Imagine a short wrestler planting both feet without moving a step.
abstract.cn: 想象一位矮壮的摔跤手双脚一扎，一步不退。

abstract.en: Think of a short thick brass stand under an old lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象旧台灯下那个又短又粗的黄铜底座。

examples.en: The farmer was stocky and used to lifting sacks all day.
examples.cn: 那位农夫身材矮壮，习惯了整天扛麻袋。

examples.en: A tall man and a stockier one carried the bench indoors.
examples.cn: 一个高个子男人和一个更矮壮些的男人把长凳抬进了屋。

examples.en: The young tree had stocky branches that held heavy fruit.
examples.cn: 这棵小树的枝条粗短，撑得住沉甸甸的果实。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「四套壳」——矮壮的人像穿了四套壳一样厚实压不扁；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 stocc（树干、木桩，经类推又指货物储备）→ 中古英语 stock（木墩、股本）+ 形容词词尾 -y → stocky，核心义「像树桩一样矮而粗壮」。

sensesIntro.en: Stocky begins with a trunk-like body, spreads to short thick shapes, and then widens to plain forceful style and to the noun for a sturdy person.
sensesIntro.cn: stocky 从树桩般的身形起步，扩展到粗短的物体，再延伸到直截了当的风格，并作名词指矮壮的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short thick trunk standing firm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一截矮而粗的树桩稳稳立着。

branches.en: The short strong body is the main sense used of people.
branches.cn: 矮而结实的身体是用人来描写的主要义项。

branches.en: The trunk image moves to limbs, tools, and plants.
branches.cn: 树桩意象转移到肢体、器具与植物上。

branches.en: Short blunt speech borrows the solid body image.
branches.cn: 简短直白的话借用了结实的身形意象。

branches.en: The adjective turns into the noun for the person himself.
branches.cn: 形容词转而成为指称本人的名词。

branches.en: Built bodies and thick bases share the same compact form.
branches.cn: 壮实的身体和粗厚的底座共享同一种紧凑造型。

intro.en: Stocky is a short adjectival formation from the stock family, enlarged by -ness and -ily.
intro.cn: stocky 是由 stock 一族构成的简短形容词，并由 -ness 与 -ily 扩展出派生词。

latinIntro.en: Stocky has no Latin source: its base is a Germanic trunk word.
latinIntro.cn: stocky 没有拉丁语来源：它的基础是日耳曼语的「树干」一词。

items.example: Stocc is the oldest visible layer.
items.exampleCN: stocc 是最古老的可见层次。

items.meaning: a trunk, a store, or shares
items.example: Stock is the noun beneath the adjective.
items.exampleCN: stock 是形容词底下的名词。

items.example: The suffix -y forms stocky.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 stocky。

items.example: Stocky describes a compact build.
items.exampleCN: stocky 描写紧凑的身架。

items.example: The comparative adds -er.
items.exampleCN: 比较级加上 -er。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms stockiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 stockiness。

items.example: Stockiness names the quality.
items.exampleCN: stockiness 指称这种性质。

items.example: Stockily built is a common phrase.
items.exampleCN: stockily built 是常见说法。

definition_zh: 仓库；货栈；宝库；知识宝库
definition_en: a building where goods are stored, or a person or thing that holds a great supply of something
core_image: 一座门板厚重、堆满货物的旧仓库
scene: 港口边那座旧石仓库里，一袋袋咖啡豆从地板一直堆到房梁。The old stone storehouse near the harbour was filled with sacks of coffee from floor to roof.
sceneCN: 这里 storehouse 是「仓库」（第 1 个义项：存放货物的建筑物）；句意：港口边那座旧石仓里，从地板到房顶都堆满了咖啡豆麻袋。

derivatives.zh: 复合词的前半部分，本身义为「储存；商店」
store 加 -age 构成，义为「储藏；仓储」
同义复合词，回译作「仓库」

senses.title: A building for storing goods
senses.definition: a large building in which goods are kept until they are needed
senses.definitionCN: 存放货物直到需要时再取用的大型建筑物
senses.example: The grain storehouse stood beside the railway.
senses.exampleCN: 那座粮仓立铁路旁边。
senses.why: Store means to keep and house means a building, so a storehouse is quite literally a keeping building.
senses.whyCN: store 意为储存，house 意为房屋，所以 storehouse 字面就是「用来保存东西的房子」。

senses.title: A rich source of knowledge
senses.definition: a person or institution that holds a great amount of information or skill
senses.definitionCN: 掌握大量信息或技能的人或机构
senses.example: The old professor is a walking storehouse of local history.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老教授是一部活的地方史宝库。
senses.why: If a building can hold grain, a mind can hold facts, so the building image turns into a metaphor for knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 房屋能存粮，头脑就能存知识，于是建筑物意象成了知识的比喻。

senses.title: A collection that preserves things
senses.definition: a place or system that keeps something valuable safe, such as a museum or a natural reserve
senses.definitionCN: 保存珍贵事物的场所或系统，如博物馆或自然保护区
senses.example: The valley is a storehouse for rare wild plants.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷是稀有野生植物的宝库。
senses.why: Keeping goods safe is not only for trade, so the same word serves museums, archives, and nature.
senses.whyCN: 安全保存物资不只为了买卖，所以同一个词也服务于博物馆、档案馆和自然。

senses.title: A person full of memories
senses.definition: a person who holds a large number of memories or stories
senses.definitionCN: 怀有大量回忆或故事的人
senses.example: Grandmother is a storehouse of family stories.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶是一部家族故事的宝库。
senses.why: The metaphor narrows from facts to feelings, so a storehouse can be the memory itself.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从知识收窄到情感，于是 storehouse 也可以指承载回忆的那一方。

senses.title: A data repository
senses.definition: a digital system that keeps large amounts of information for later use
senses.definitionCN: 保存大量信息以备后用的电子系统
senses.example: The lab built a storehouse of climate records.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室建起了一个气候记录数据仓库。
senses.why: Modern storage moves from brick walls to hard drives, but the keeping function stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 现代储存从砖墙搬到了硬盘，但「保存」这一功能丝毫未变。

intro.en: Storehouse joins store, from Old French estor, a supply, and house, from Old English hus, a dwelling.
intro.cn: storehouse 由 store（来自古法语 estor，供给）与 house（来自古英语 hus，住所）复合而成。

items.en: Hus means a house or shelter, and forms compounds freely.
items.cn: 古英语 hus 意为房屋或遮蔽之处，能自由构成复合词。

items.en: Estor means a supply or provision made ready.
items.cn: 古法语 estor 意为备好的供给或物资。

items.en: Store enters English as a supply kept for future use.
items.cn: store 进入英语，指为将来使用而保存的物资。

items.en: Storehouse is recorded as a compound for a building that holds supplies.
items.cn: storehouse 作为复合词首次见于记录，指存放物资的房屋。

items.en: The word extends from warehouses to figurative treasuries of knowledge.
items.cn: 这个词从货栈扩展到比喻意义上的知识与珍藏宝库。

note.en: Storehouse pairs the store family with the house family and sits near practical storage and treasury words.
note.cn: storehouse 把 store 一族与 house 一族配在一起，并与实用的储存词和「宝库」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to keep something for later, or a shop
the act or space of keeping things
the levels of a building
entries.definitionCN: 楼房的层数，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a large building for storing goods for trade
entries.definitionCN: 存放贸易货物的大仓库

entries.definition: a place where supplies or vehicles are kept
a place where valuable things are kept

normalIntro.en: Storehouse is a textbook compound: a house for storing things, and by extension a mind full of them.
normalIntro.cn: storehouse 是教科书式的复合词：存东西的房子，引申为装满东西的头脑。

normal.en: Store means to keep and house means a building, so the word explains itself.
normal.cn: store 是储存，house 是房屋，这个词自己就把意思说清楚了。

normal.en: A storehouse of knowledge describes a learned person.
normal.cn: a storehouse of knowledge 用来形容学识渊博的人。

normal.en: The plural storehouses keeps the compound as one word.
normal.cn: 复数 storehouses 仍把复合词写成一个词。

normal.en: Warehouse is the commercial cousin with a different first half.
normal.cn: warehouse 是换了前半部分的商业近亲。

normal.en: Storage names the activity, storehouse names the building.
normal.cn: storage 指储存这件事，storehouse 指储存的建筑物。

abstract.en: Picture a thick wooden door opening onto sacks stacked to the rafters.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇厚重的木门打开，里面是堆到房梁的麻袋。

abstract.en: Imagine an old professor whose head overflows with dates and stories.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老教授，脑子里塞满了年份和故事。

abstract.en: Think of a museum basement holding treasures nobody may touch.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆地下室里存放着无人可碰的珍宝。

examples.en: The spice storehouse was cool and dry all year.
examples.cn: 那座香料仓库一年到头都凉爽干燥。

examples.en: Her diary became a storehouse of childhood memories.
examples.cn: 她的日记成了一座童年记忆的宝库。

examples.en: Local volunteers turned the barn into a storehouse for flood supplies.
examples.cn: 当地志愿者把谷仓改成了防汛物资仓库。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯托豪斯」——斯托先生的家（豪斯）就是仓库；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hus（房屋）+ 古法语 estor（供给）→ 中古英语 store（储备）+ house → storehouse，核心义「存放东西的房屋」。

sensesIntro.en: Storehouse starts as a building that holds goods, becomes a metaphor for knowledge, then for preserved treasures, memories, and finally digital data.
sensesIntro.cn: storehouse 先是存放货物的建筑，再成为知识的比喻，然后是珍存之物、回忆，最后是数字数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stout door opening onto stacked sacks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇厚重的大门后堆满麻袋。

branches.en: A building for goods is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 存放货物的建筑是字面义项。

branches.en: A learned person is a living building of facts.
branches.cn: 博览群书的人就是一座活的事实仓库。

branches.en: Museums and reserves keep treasures rather than trade goods.
branches.cn: 博物馆与保护区保存的是宝物而非贸易货物。

branches.en: Facts and memories are both things held inside a person.
branches.cn: 事实与回忆都是被保存在人内心里的东西。

branches.en: A digital store keeps records just as a barn keeps grain.
branches.cn: 数字仓库保存记录，正像谷仓保存粮食。

intro.en: Storehouse is a two-part English compound, with store and storage forming the core of its word family.
intro.cn: storehouse 是由两部分构成的英语复合词，store 与 storage 构成其词族核心。

latinIntro.en: The store half comes through Old French from Latin instaurare, to restore or set up, while house is purely Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: store 这一半经古法语上溯到拉丁语 instaurare（恢复、设立），而 house 则纯粹是日耳曼语源。

items.example: Hus supplies the second half.
items.exampleCN: hus 提供后半部分。

items.example: Estor supplies the first half.
items.exampleCN: estor 提供前半部分。

items.example: Store is the base word.
items.exampleCN: store 是基础词。

items.example: House completes the compound.
items.exampleCN: house 补全了这个复合词。

items.example: Storehouse combines both halves.
items.exampleCN: storehouse 合并两部分。

items.example: The plural adds -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数加上 -s。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或场所的词尾
items.example: The suffix -age forms storage.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -age 构成 storage。

items.example: Storage names the activity.
items.exampleCN: storage 指称储存这件事。

items.example: Warehouse is the close synonym.
items.exampleCN: warehouse 是近义复合词。

definition_zh: 楼层；层；房屋的一层
definition_en: one level of a building, usually one floor
core_image: 一栋楼被横向切开，像千层糕一样叠起一层层空间
scene: 公寓电梯的按钮上，第三层标在最上面。The lift panel showed that our flat was on the top storey of the block.
sceneCN: 这里 storey 是「楼层」（第 1 个义项：建筑物的一层）；句意：电梯面板显示我们的公寓在这栋楼的最高一层。

derivatives.zh: 由 storey 加 -ed 构成，义为「有若干层的」，多与数词连用
由 multi-（多）与 storey 复合而成，义为「多层的」
storey 的美式拼写复数形式，义为「若干层楼」

senses.title: One level of a building
senses.definition: a level or floor of a building, counted from the ground up
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物自地面往上数的一层或一个楼层
senses.example: The library has three storeys and a basement.
senses.exampleCN: 这座图书馆有三层外加一个地下室。
senses.why: The word pictures buildings as stacked layers, so a storey is one layer of that stack.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把建筑想成立起来的一叠层，所以一层就是这叠层中的一片。

senses.title: Used in compound descriptions
senses.definition: used after a number or adjective to describe how many levels a building has
senses.definitionCN: 跟在数词或形容词后，说明建筑一共有几层
senses.example: They moved into a two-storey house near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬进了河边一栋两层楼的房子。
senses.why: Once a storey is a countable layer, it easily becomes a unit for measuring height.
senses.whyCN: 既然一层是可数的层片，它自然就成了衡量建筑高度的单位。

senses.title: Head and story contrast
senses.definition: an informal way of referring to a person mind or mental balance
senses.definitionCN: 对某人头脑或精神状态的俗称用法
senses.example: After the accident he was clearly several storeys short.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，他很明显脑子不太正常。
senses.why: Because floors are stacked high, people describe a troubled mind as not having all floors in place.
senses.whyCN: 因为楼层是层层叠高的，人们就把精神不正常比作楼层没有凑齐。

intro.en: Storey comes from Anglo-Latin historia, which meant a tier of painted windows or a row of carvings on an old building, probably from story in the sense of a painted scene.
intro.cn: storey 来自中世纪拉丁语 historia，原指古建筑上一排彩绘窗或一层雕刻，一般认为源于 story（绘制的故事画面）一词。

items.en: Historia means a narrative or a picture telling a story.
items.cn: historia 意为叙述，也指讲述故事的图画。

items.en: In building records historia means a tier of windows with painted history.
items.cn: 在建筑记录中，historia 指一排绘有故事画的窗户。

items.en: Storey names a row of windows or carvings on a wall.
items.cn: 中古英语 storey 指墙上一排窗或一层雕刻。

items.en: The meaning grows into one complete level of a building.
items.cn: 词义扩展为建筑完整的一层。

items.en: Britons keep storey while Americans settle on story.
items.cn: 英国人保留 storey 拼写，美国人则定型为 story。

items.en: Modern English uses storey mainly in compounds such as multi-storey.
items.cn: 现代英语中 storey 多用于 multi-storey 这类复合词。

note.en: Storey is the British noun for a building level; its look-alikes sit in the store and stair families, and its near meanings are other floor words.
note.cn: storey 是表示「楼层」的英式名词；形近词集中在 store 与 stair 词族，近义词则是其他表示「层」的说法。

entries.definition: the American spelling of storey, and also a tale
entries.definitionCN: storey 的美式拼写；同时也表示「故事」，要注意区分

entries.definition: the plural of storey
a shop or a supply kept for later
entries.definitionCN: 商店或储备；与 storey 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a level of a building, or the surface we walk on
entries.definitionCN: 楼层；也可以指可以行走的地面

entries.definition: a height or a horizontal tier
entries.definitionCN: 高度层；常用于建筑与工程说明

entries.definition: a floor of a ship or bus
entries.definitionCN: 船舶或车辆的一层甲板

normalIntro.en: Storey is the building word, not the tale word: one storey is one layer of a house.
normalIntro.cn: storey 是建筑用词，不是「故事」那个词：一层楼就是一叠层中的一层。

normal.en: A two-storey house has floors on two levels.
normal.cn: 两层的房子有两个高度上的楼层。

normal.en: Multi-storey car parks stack cars on several floors.
normal.cn: 多层停车场把车停在不同楼层的车库里。

normal.en: Remember the e in storey: that e marks the British building word.
normal.cn: 记住 storey 里的字母 e：这个 e 标记的是英式建筑用词。

normal.en: Write the plural storeys in British style, stories in American style.
normal.cn: 英式复数写 storeys，美式复数写 stories。

normal.en: Compare floor: floor also means the surface you walk on, storey only means the level.
normal.cn: 对比 floor：floor 还指可走的地面，storey 只指楼层。

abstract.en: Picture a cake cut crosswise, each slice a storey.
abstract.cn: 想象把一栋楼横切成蛋糕，每片就是一层。

abstract.en: Imagine counting windows in rows, one row for each storey.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排数窗户，每一排对应一层楼。

abstract.en: See a lift panel with buttons stacked like a ladder.
abstract.cn: 想象电梯面板上的按钮像梯子一样叠上去。

examples.en: The old warehouse had five storeys and narrow windows.
examples.cn: 那座老仓库有五层，窗户很窄。

examples.en: Regulations require a lift in any building above three storeys.
examples.cn: 规定要求超过三层的建筑都要装电梯。

examples.en: Their flat sits on the upper storey of a quiet terrace.
examples.cn: 他们的公寓位于一排安静联排房屋的上层。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「楼层」谐音「斯托里」——先把 storey 听成「一层层摞起来的故事」；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 historia（叙述；绘有故事的图画）→ 中世纪拉丁语 historia（建筑上一排彩绘窗）→ 中古英语 storey（一排窗）→ 一层楼；核心义「叠起来的层」。

sensesIntro.en: Storey starts as one level of a building, extends to a compound form that measures height, and survives in an informal image of the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: storey 先从「建筑的一层」起步，再发展为衡量层高的复合用法，还留有一个形容头脑的口语比喻义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a building sliced into stacked layers, like a layer cake.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋楼被横切成叠起的层片，像千层糕。

branches.en: One concrete layer of a building is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 建筑中具体的一层是日常义项。

branches.en: The compound use turns the layer into a unit of height.
branches.cn: 复合用法把「层」变成衡量建筑高度的单位。

branches.en: The playful mind sense borrows the stacked-floors picture.
branches.cn: 口语里形容头脑的义项借用了楼层堆叠的画面。

branches.en: A single storey and a two-storey house share the same layer count.
branches.cn: 单层的层与两层的房子共用同一个层数概念。

branches.en: Both a floor and a minded person are spoken of in layers.
branches.cn: 楼层和人的头脑都可以用「层」来打比方。

intro.en: Storey is a short rootless word; its growth comes from compounding, from storey formed compounds, and from the -ed adjective storeyed.
intro.cn: storey 是一个短小的词，它的扩展主要靠复合构词：与数词组合成 storey 构成的复合词，以及加 -ed 构成形容词 storeyed。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin ancestor is historia, a narrative or painted scene that named a tier of windows.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁语祖先是 historia，意为叙述或绘制的故事画面，最初用来指一排窗户。

items.example: Historia supplies the first image of painted tiers.
items.exampleCN: historia 提供了「彩绘层带」的最初意象。

items.example: Storey is the British noun for a floor.
items.exampleCN: storey 是英式表示楼层的名词。

items.example: The prefix multi- builds multi-storey.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 multi- 构成 multi-storey。

items.example: The count two forms two-storey.
items.exampleCN: 数词构成 two-storey。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms storeyed.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 storeyed。

items.meaning: having the stated number of storeys
items.example: Storeyed is used in phrases such as a three storeyed tower.
items.exampleCN: storeyed 用在三层的塔这类短语里。

items.example: The suffix -s forms the plural storeys.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成复数 storeys。

items.example: American English writes story for a floor.
items.exampleCN: 美式英语用 story 表示楼层。

items.example: The adjective top forms top storey.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 top 构成 top storey。

latinEntries.meaning: tiers of painted windows in records
latinEntries.meaningCN: 建筑记录中的彩绘窗层

definition_zh: 故事情节；情节主线；剧情线
definition_en: the main series of events in a story, film, or book
core_image: 一条线把散落的场景与人物串成一串，最后收成完整的形状
scene: 影评人说这部电影的画面漂亮，可惜情节太弱。The critic praised the visuals but found the storyline thin and predictable.
sceneCN: 这里 storyline 是「情节主线」（第 1 个义项：故事的整条情节线）；句意：影评人称赞画面，却觉得情节单薄又老套。

pos.zh: 故事情节；情节主线；剧情线

derivatives.zh: storyline 的核心前置词，由 story（故事）与 line（线）复合而来，义为「故事」
由 story 加 teller（讲述者）构成，义为「讲故事的人」
由 story 加 board（画板）再加 -ing 构成，义为「分镜脚本绘制」

senses.title: The main line of events
senses.definition: the sequence of events that makes up the main plot of a book, film, or play
senses.definitionCN: 构成书、电影或戏剧主要情节的事件序列
senses.example: The novel has a simple storyline but rich characters.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说情节简单，人物却很丰满。
senses.why: A line is a single continuous thread, so the word names the thread that runs through all the events.
senses.whyCN: line 是一条连续不断的线，所以这个词指穿起全部事件的这条主线。

senses.title: The plot of a game or series
senses.definition: the connected narrative that players or viewers follow through levels, episodes, or seasons
senses.definitionCN: 玩家或观众随着关卡、剧集或季度推进而跟随的连贯叙事
senses.example: Each expansion adds a new storyline to the game.
senses.exampleCN: 每个扩展包都给这款游戏加入一条新剧情线。
senses.why: When a story is split across levels or episodes, a single line still holds the parts together as one journey.
senses.whyCN: 当故事被拆进多个关卡或剧集时，仍有一条线把各部分串成一段完整旅程。

senses.title: A planned narrative course
senses.definition: an intended direction for a story planned by writers or teachers before telling it
senses.definitionCN: 作者或教师在讲述前预先设定好的故事走向
senses.example: Teachers built their lessons around the storyline of a village festival.
senses.exampleCN: 老师们围绕一个乡村节日的剧情线来设计课程。
senses.why: A planned line lets many scenes share one track, so the word also names the intended route of a narrative.
senses.whyCN: 事先画好的线让众多场景共享同一条轨，所以这个词也指叙事预设的走向。

intro.en: Storyline is a modern English compound of story and line, recorded from the middle of the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: storyline 是现代英语的复合词，由 story 与 line 组合而成，一般认为首见于十九世纪中叶。

items.en: Historia means a narrative or an account of events.
items.cn: historia 意为叙述或对事件的陈述。

items.en: Estoire carries the sense of a written tale.
items.cn: estoire 承载「成文故事」的含义。

items.en: Story is established as an account or a tale.
items.cn: 中古英语中 story 已确立为「叙述、故事」之义。

items.en: Line comes through Latin linea, a linen thread, and Old English line.
items.cn: line 经拉丁语 linea（亚麻线）进入古英语 line。

items.en: The two words combine as storyline, the thread of a plot.
items.cn: 两词组合成 storyline，指情节的线索。

items.en: Film, television, and games widen it to any narrative path.
items.cn: 电影、电视与游戏把它扩展到一切叙事路径。

note.en: Storyline sits in the story word family and close to other plot words that describe how events are arranged.
note.cn: storyline 属于 story 词族，并与其他描述事件编排方式的「情节」词相邻。

entries.definition: an account of real or imagined events
entries.definitionCN: 对真实或想象事件的讲述

entries.definition: a person who tells or writes stories
a brief plan with main points only
entries.definitionCN: 只列要点的提纲；与 storyline 共享 line 一词

entries.definition: the main events of a story with their causes and links
entries.definitionCN: 故事主要事件及其因果与关联

entries.definition: a connected account of events
a written outline of a scene sequence

normalIntro.en: Storyline is a picture word: the line that runs through a story holds its events in order.
normalIntro.cn: storyline 是个画面词：穿过故事的那条线把事件按顺序串起来。

normal.en: A weak storyline means the plot line sags.
normal.cn: a weak storyline 指情节主线松散无力。

normal.en: Follow a storyline means to keep track of events.
normal.cn: follow a storyline 指顺着事件看下去。

normal.en: The plural is storylines, one storyline per season.
normal.cn: 复数是 storylines，每一季有一条情节线。

normal.en: Split it as story plus line: the story given a line.
normal.cn: 拆成 story 加 line：给故事画一条线。

normal.en: Compare plot: plot stresses causes, storyline stresses the flow of events.
normal.cn: 对比 plot：plot 强调因果，storyline 强调事件的流向。

abstract.en: See beads on a string, each bead one scene.
abstract.cn: 想象一串珠子，每颗珠子是一个场景。

abstract.en: Picture a red thread traced over a page of scripts.
abstract.cn: 想象在剧本页上被红笔一路画出的一条线。

abstract.en: Imagine a train track joining scattered stations.
abstract.cn: 想象铁轨把散落的车站连成一条路。

examples.en: Critics praised the acting but complained about the confusing storyline.
examples.cn: 评论家称赞演技，却抱怨情节线令人困惑。

examples.en: The sequel continues the storyline from the earlier film.
examples.cn: 续集延续了前一部电影的情节主线。

examples.en: Good videogames use the storyline to keep players moving forward.
examples.cn: 优秀的电子游戏用剧情线推动玩家不断前进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「故事来」——故事一层层「来」到眼前，连起来就是一条线；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: story（拉丁语 historia、古法语 estoire：故事）+ line（拉丁语 linea：亚麻线）→ 现代英语 storyline：贯穿故事的那条线。

sensesIntro.en: Storyline begins as the main thread of a fiction plot, then covers interactive and episodic narratives, and finally a planned narrative route.
sensesIntro.cn: storyline 先指虚构作品情节的主线，再涵盖互动与分集叙事，最后指事先规划的叙事走向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread that joins scattered scenes into one continuous shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把散落场景连成连续形状的线。

branches.en: The main plot thread of a book or film is the central sense.
branches.cn: 书或电影的主要情节线是核心义项。

branches.en: Games and series stretch the line across levels and seasons.
branches.cn: 游戏与剧集把这条线拉过关卡与季度。

branches.en: A planned route is the intended version of the line.
branches.cn: 预先设定的走向就是这条线被规划好的样子。

branches.en: A plot and a game narrative both rely on one drawing thread.
branches.cn: 情节与游戏叙事都依赖同一条牵引线。

branches.en: Writers plan a route and players follow it level by level.
branches.cn: 作者规划路线，玩家则一关一关地跟随。

intro.en: Storyline is a two-part compound: story from Latin historia and line from Latin linea, with English derivatives built on story.
intro.cn: storyline 是双成分复合词：story 源自拉丁语 historia，line 源自拉丁语 linea；英语另以 story 为基础构词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin sources are historia for story and linea for line, each keeping its own thread of meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源分别是表示故事的 historia 与表示线的 linea，各自保留了自己的语义脉络。

items.example: Story is the first half of storyline.
items.exampleCN: story 是 storyline 的前半部分。

items.meaning: a long thin mark or thread
items.example: Line is the second half of storyline.
items.exampleCN: line 是 storyline 的后半部分。

items.example: Storyteller joins story with teller.
items.exampleCN: storyteller 把 story 与 teller 组合起来。

items.example: The element -board builds storyboard.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -board 构成 storyboard。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms storytelling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 storytelling。

items.example: The prefix multi- forms multi-strand storylines.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 multi- 构成 multi-strand storylines。

items.example: The suffix -s forms storylines.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成 storylines。

items.example: The suffix -less gives storyless in rare use.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 在罕见用法中构成 storyless。

items.example: The prefix sub- labels a subplot, a secondary storyline.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 用来标出副线情节。

definition_zh: 胖胖的；结实的；粗壮有力的；坚定的；烈性黑啤酒
definition_en: thick and strong in body or build, firm in purpose, or a dark heavy beer
core_image: 一截粗壮的木桩，短而结实，怎么推都不倒
scene: 老村口那棵树下，木桩被磨得发亮，依然稳稳扎在地里。The old gatepost was stout and had held firm for a century.
sceneCN: 这里 stout 是「结实的、粗壮的」（第 1 个义项：形体厚重结实）；句意：那根旧门柱结实粗壮，牢固地立了一百年。

pos.zh: 胖胖的；结实的；粗壮的；坚定的；顽强的

collocations.zh: 坚决的辩护；牢固的防御

derivatives.zh: 由 stout 加 -ly 构成，义为「坚决地；顽强力强地」
由 stout 加 -ness 构成，义为「粗壮；坚定」
由 stout 与 hearted（有心的）复合而成，义为「勇敢的；无畏的」

senses.title: Thick and strongly built
senses.definition: fairly thick in body or build, and therefore strong
senses.definitionCN: 身板或构件较厚实，因而很结实
senses.example: He wore stout boots for the mountain walk.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着结实的靴子去走山路。
senses.why: The core image is a short thick post, so stout first describes solid, strong build.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一根短而粗的木桩，所以 stout 首先形容厚实、结实的身形或物件。

senses.title: Firm and determined
senses.definition: very determined, loyal, or strong in the face of opposition
senses.definitionCN: 面对阻力时非常坚决、忠诚或顽强
senses.example: The committee put up stout resistance to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会对这个计划进行了顽强抵抗。
senses.why: A thick solid thing cannot easily be pushed over, so the physical strength becomes moral firmness.
senses.whyCN: 厚实坚固的东西不容易被推倒，于是身体上的结实变成了精神上的坚定。

senses.title: A dark heavy beer
senses.definition: a strong dark beer made with roasted malt
senses.definitionCN: 用烘烤麦芽酿成的深色浓烈啤酒
senses.example: He ordered a glass of stout with his dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯黑啤配晚餐。
senses.why: A heavy strong drink is stout in the sense of solid and powerful, so the beer takes the same label.
senses.whyCN: 浓烈厚重的酒在「扎实、有劲」这层意义上也是 stout，于是啤酒沿用了这个标签。

intro.en: Stout comes from Old French estout, bold or proud, from a Germanic source; its spelling and meaning settled in Middle English.
intro.cn: stout 来自古法语 estout（勇敢、骄傲），源于日耳曼语；其拼写与词义在中古英语中定型。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic root, probably *stolt, meant proud or bold.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个日耳曼语词根，意为骄傲、大胆（重构形式）。

items.en: Frankish carries the word into northern France.
items.cn: 法兰克语把这个词带入法国北部。

items.en: Estout means proud, fierce, or brave.
items.cn: estout 意为骄傲、凶猛、勇敢。

items.en: Stout shifts from proud to strong, bold, and thick-set.
items.cn: 中古英语中 stout 从「骄傲」转向「强壮、胆大、粗壮」。

items.en: Brewers borrow stout to name a strong dark beer.
items.cn: 酿造商借用 stout 来称一种浓烈的深色啤酒。

items.en: Modern English keeps stout for build, courage, and the drink.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 stout 的体形、勇气与啤酒三种用法。

note.en: Stout looks like other st- words of strength and sits near adjectives for a full body or a firm will.
note.cn: stout 与其它表示强壮的 st- 开头词形近，在意义上则与形容体形丰满或意志坚定的词相邻。

entries.definition: in a firm and determined way
the quality of being thick or firm
very brave and bold
strong and unlikely to break
entries.definitionCN: 坚固耐用的；与 stout 常可互换

entries.definition: slightly fat in a pleasant way
firmly determined
entries.definitionCN: 坚决果断的；对应 stout 的坚定义

normalIntro.en: Stout starts from a short thick post: strength of body first, then strength of will.
normalIntro.cn: stout 从一根短粗的木桩出发：先是身体的结实，再是意志的坚定。

normal.en: Stout shoes are thick and walk far.
normal.cn: stout shoes 指结实的鞋子，能走很远。

normal.en: Stout resistance is firm refusal to give way.
normal.cn: stout resistance 是坚决不退让的抵抗。

normal.en: The adverb form stoutly keeps the firm meaning.
normal.cn: 副词 stoutly 保留了「坚决」这层意思。

normal.en: As a noun, stout is a strong dark beer.
normal.cn: 作名词时 stout 指浓烈的黑啤酒。

normal.en: Compare sturdy: sturdy stresses not breaking, stout stresses thick and strong.
normal.cn: 对比 sturdy：sturdy 强调不易坏，stout 强调厚实有劲。

abstract.en: Picture a thick fence post worn smooth by hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被手摸得发亮的粗栅栏桩。

abstract.en: See a heavy tumbler of dark beer, thick in the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯沉甸甸的黑啤酒，杯里浓稠厚重。

abstract.en: Imagine a short wrestler who will not move when pushed.
abstract.cn: 想象一位矮壮的摔跤手，被人推也纹丝不动。

examples.en: The cottage was built from stout oak beams.
examples.cn: 这座小屋是用结实的橡木梁建成的。

examples.en: She made a stout defence of her colleague.
examples.cn: 她坚决为同事辩护。

examples.en: The pub serves a pale ale and a dark stout.
examples.cn: 这家酒馆供应淡色麦酒和深色黑啤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯涛特」——听起来像「死掏特」，狠掏一把力，所以结实又有劲；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 estout（骄傲、勇敢），一般认为源自日耳曼语词根（重构形式），原义「骄傲」→「强壮、胆大」→「粗壮结实」→「坚定」→ 烈性黑啤酒。

sensesIntro.en: Stout moves from a thick strong body, to a firm will, and finally to a dark heavy beer.
sensesIntro.cn: stout 从厚实强壮的身体，转到坚定的意志，最后落到一种浓稠的深色啤酒上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short thick post that stays upright however hard it is pushed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根短粗的木桩，怎么推都稳稳立着。

branches.en: A thick strong build is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 厚实强壮的身形是身体层面的义项。

branches.en: A will that will not bend is the moral sense.
branches.cn: 不肯弯的意志是精神层面的义项。

branches.en: A dark heavy drink takes the label of solid strength.
branches.cn: 浓烈厚重的酒借用了「扎实有力」这个标签。

branches.en: A stout body and a stout heart are both hard to push over.
branches.cn: 结实的身体与坚定的心都很难被推倒。

branches.en: Both thick boots and thick beer are stout in the sense of solid.
branches.cn: 厚实的靴子和浓稠的啤酒在「扎实」这层意义上都是 stout。

intro.en: Stout is a word without a Latin affix structure; its family grows with -ly, -ness, and hearted compounds.
intro.cn: stout 本身没有拉丁词缀结构，它的词族靠 -ly、-ness 与 hearted 复合而成。

latinIntro.en: Stout has no Latin ancestor; it entered English through Old French, so few Latin cognates are listed.
latinIntro.cn: stout 没有拉丁语祖先，它经由古法语进入英语，因此拉丁同源词很少列出。

items.example: Stout is the base adjective.
items.exampleCN: stout 是基础形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms stoutly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 stoutly。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms stoutness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 stoutness。

items.meaning: having the stated kind of heart
items.example: The element -hearted forms stouthearted.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -hearted 构成 stouthearted。

items.example: The suffix -er forms stouter.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 stouter。

items.example: The suffix -est forms stoutest.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -est 构成 stoutest。

items.example: Estout is the Old French ancestor of stout.
items.exampleCN: estout 是 stout 的古法语祖先。

items.example: The suffix -s forms the beer noun stouts.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成啤酒名词的复数 stouts。

items.example: Prefixes such as un- are rarely used with stout.
items.exampleCN: un- 这类前缀很少与 stout 组合。
